examples.translation: Der Post-Messzustand von $\mathsf{X}$ ergibt sich durch Normierung des Vektors $\Pi_a\vert\psi\rangle$, den wir hier jedoch noch ignorieren.
examples.why: Both candidate antecedents are masculine, so "den" reads most naturally as referring to the vector rather than to the post-measurement state — the English is explicit about which is being set aside.

examples.source: Each outcome a appears with probability p(a) = Tr(…).
examples.suggested: Jedes Ergebnis $a$ tritt mit der folgenden Wahrscheinlichkeit auf: [display equation]
examples.translation: Jedes Ergebnis $a$ tritt mit Wahrscheinlichkeit [display equation] auf.
examples.why: The separable particle "auf." is stranded on its own line after the display block and will render as a one-word paragraph; recast so the sentence closes before the equation.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no semantic drift, no dropped caveats, informal "tú" holds consistently ("te guía", "notarás", "si quieres profundizar"). The real defect is a glossary leak: the everyday terms "circuit" and "gate" are left as capitalized English nouns inside Spanish prose — "tu primer Circuit cuántico", "estados cuánticos, Gates y Circuits", "compilando Circuits cuánticos", "Circuits cuánticos parametrizados" — while the same file correctly writes "el tiempo para ejecutar un circuito" and "códigos de corrección de errores", so "circuito" and "Circuit" split within one lesson. Worst instance is the CLOPS expansion, rendered "Operaciones por Capa de Circuit por Segundo", which is both leaked and ungrammatical (double "por"); it should read "Operaciones de Capa de Circuito por Segundo". Two smaller native-editor fixes: "Otro componente crítico al que apuntamos" is a calque of "we point to", and "computadoras tradicionales y clásicas" turns English's appositive "traditional, classical computers" into two distinct kinds of machine.

examples.source: You began this course by diving right into running your first quantum circuit, and learning how the laws of quantum mechanics are used to create quantum states, gates, and circuits.
examples.suggested: ...a ejecutar tu primer circuito cuántico y aprendiendo cómo las leyes de la mecánica cuántica se usan para crear estados cuánticos, compuertas y circuitos.
examples.translation: Comenzaste este curso lanzándote directamente a ejecutar tu primer Circuit cuántico y aprendiendo cómo las leyes de la mecánica cuántica se usan para crear estados cuánticos, Gates y Circuits.
examples.why: Untranslated capitalized English 'Circuit'/'Gates' inside Spanish prose. Both terms have settled Spanish renderings (circuito, compuerta/puerta), and the same file already uses 'circuito' in the CLOPS paragraph, so the file contradicts itself on its most basic vocabulary.

examples.source: To measure speed we use something called Circuit Layer Operations per Second (CLOPS).
examples.suggested: Para medir la velocidad usamos algo llamado Operaciones de Capa de Circuito por Segundo (CLOPS, por sus siglas en inglés).
examples.translation: Para medir la velocidad, usamos algo llamado Operaciones por Capa de Circuit por Segundo (CLOPS, por sus siglas en inglés).
examples.why: Same leak, plus the expansion is ungrammatical: 'por Capa de Circuit por Segundo' repeats 'por' and misparses 'Circuit Layer' as a rate. A learner meeting CLOPS for the first time gets a garbled acronym expansion.

examples.source: Another critical component we point to when we look to see how quantum computers are improving is speed.
examples.suggested: Otro componente crítico que tenemos en cuenta al evaluar cómo mejoran las computadoras cuánticas es la velocidad.
examples.translation: Otro componente crítico al que apuntamos cuando observamos cómo mejoran las computadoras cuánticas es la velocidad.
examples.why: 'al que apuntamos' is a word-for-word calque of 'we point to'; in Spanish 'apuntar a' reads as aiming at a target, not as citing a metric. A native technical writer would say 'que tenemos en cuenta' or 'al que recurrimos'.

examples.source: Quantum computing is not going to replace traditional, classical computers
examples.suggested: La computación cuántica no va a reemplazar a las computadoras clásicas tradicionales
examples.translation: La computación cuántica no va a reemplazar a las computadoras tradicionales y clásicas
examples.why: English uses an appositive: 'traditional' and 'classical' describe the same machines. The 'y' makes them read as two separate categories, subtly implying there exist traditional-but-not-classical computers. Not misleading enough to fail, but a native editor would drop the conjunction.

editor_note: The prose is otherwise faithful, informal-"tú" throughout ("establece el indicador experimental", "obtén el tiempo de la programación", "conviértelos a circuits ISA") and the technical explanations (canal de excitación (drive), ciclo de programación, difusión/determinación de ramas) are accurate. Two things a native technical editor would change. First, "circuit" is left as the raw English noun everywhere and inflected as if it were Spanish — "el tiempo de los circuits", "circuits estáticos", "circuits dinámicos", "los datos de tiempo del circuit", "conviértelos a circuits ISA"; "circuito(s)" is the universal Spanish term in this field and the English form reads as a glossary keep-English leak, not a convention. Second, in Próximos pasos "Classical feedforward" is rendered "Retroalimentación clásica", i.e. *feedback*, which names the opposite direction of information flow from feedforward (the correct rendering is "prealimentación clásica" or keeping "feedforward"); the parenthetical "(circuits dinámicos)" is what keeps it from actively misteaching. Third, minor: the title/description turn the English singular "circuit timing" into a plural ("el tiempo de los circuits") and "the primitive job" becomes the calque "el trabajo primitivo" rather than "el trabajo del primitivo".

examples.source: [Classical feedforward and control flow](/guides/classical-feedforward-and-control-flow) (dynamic circuits)
examples.suggested: [Prealimentación clásica (feedforward) y flujo de control](...) (circuitos dinámicos)
examples.translation: [Retroalimentación clásica y flujo de control](/guides/classical-feedforward-and-control-flow) (circuits dinámicos)
examples.why: 'Retroalimentación' is feedback — the opposite information direction from feedforward. In dynamic circuits the point is that a measurement result is fed FORWARD to condition a later gate, not looped back; the Spanish label names a different control concept.

examples.source: While the timeline drawer built in to Qiskit is useful for static circuits, it might not accurately reflect the timing of dynamic circuits
examples.suggested: ...es útil para circuitos estáticos, es posible que no refleje con precisión el tiempo de los circuitos dinámicos
examples.translation: Aunque el visualizador de línea de tiempo integrado en Qiskit es útil para circuits estáticos, es posible que no refleje con precisión el tiempo de los circuits dinámicos
examples.why: 'circuit' is left in English and inflected with Spanish adjectives file-wide (los circuits, circuits estáticos/dinámicos, del circuit, circuits ISA). 'Circuito' is the settled Spanish domain term; the English form reads as a leak and is jarring for a native reader, though still recognizable.

examples.source: set the experimental `scheduler_timing` flag to `True` when running the primitive job
examples.suggested: ...al ejecutar el trabajo del primitivo
examples.translation: establece el indicador experimental `scheduler_timing` en `True` al ejecutar el trabajo primitivo
examples.why: 'el trabajo primitivo' calques the English noun-adjunct and reads as 'the primitive/rudimentary job'; in Spanish the Qiskit primitives are 'los primitivos', so the job belongs to the primitive ('el trabajo del primitivo').

examples.source: title: "Visualize circuit timing" / "Visualize the timing of generated circuits..."
examples.suggested: "Visualizar la temporización del circuito" / "Visualiza la temporización de los circuitos generados creando una figura..."
examples.translation: "Visualizar el tiempo de los circuits" / "Visualiza el tiempo de los circuits generados generando una figura..."
examples.why: Minor: the English page title is singular ('circuit timing'), and 'generados generando' repeats the same root twice in a row, which a Spanish editor would break up ('creando'/'produciendo').

editor_note: Nothing misleading: meaning tracks the English sentence by sentence (sampling overhead $9^3$/729, depth 103→46, "réduite de plus de la moitié", the Step-2/Step-4 relevance of gate cutting), core terms are correct and consistent ("valeurs d'espérance", "distribution de quasi-probabilité conjointe", "circuit transpilé", "surcoût d'échantillonnage", backend/Sampler/QPD kept in English), and the informal "tu" holds throughout ("assure-toi", "consulte", "Réponds", "Ton temps d'exécution"). The one thing a native technical editor would change is the head term: "circuit cutting" / "gate cutting" are rendered "coupe de circuits" / "coupe de portes" (title, Background, Step 1, and the $9^3$ paragraph), where the conventional French in this field is "découpage de circuits" / "découpage de portes" — "coupe" is recognizable but reads as an awkward nominalization and brushes against the everyday electrical sense of "coupe-circuit" (fuse). Secondary: the coupling-map alt text adds "par des portes SWAP", a specification the English ("the qubits that will need to be swapped") does not make — accurate, but an unnecessary over-translation.

examples.source: Circuit cutting for depth reduction / For more in-depth discussion on circuit cutting … / Gate cutting is relevant for Steps 2 and 4
examples.suggested: Découpage de circuits pour la réduction de profondeur / … sur le découpage de circuits … / Le découpage de portes est pertinent pour les étapes 2 et 4
examples.translation: Coupe de circuits pour la réduction de profondeur / Pour une discussion plus approfondie sur la coupe de circuits … / La coupe de portes est pertinente pour les étapes 2 et 4
examples.why: "Découpage de circuits" is the established French rendering of circuit cutting in the quantum literature; "coupe" is an unidiomatic nominalization here and evokes "coupe-circuit" (electrical fuse). Consistent within the file and still recognizable, so MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: Coupling map showing the qubits that will need to be swapped
examples.suggested: Carte de couplage montrant les qubits qui devront être échangés
examples.translation: Carte de couplage montrant les qubits qui devront être échangés par des portes SWAP
examples.why: Adds "par des portes SWAP", a mechanism the English alt text leaves unstated. It happens to be true in context, so no learner is misled, but it is an addition a technical editor would trim.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveat, no inverted condition; the tricky sentences ("elle reçoit la valeur spéciale `Unset` et la valeur par défaut du serveur est utilisée", "La primitive en fait une copie, ce qui signifie que modifier le dictionnaire ou l'instance d'options d'origine n'affecte pas les options dont la primitive est propriétaire") are accurate and readable, and the informal "tu" holds in every paragraph with no vous/votre/veuillez slip. Two editorial nits remain. (1) Line 41 "Lors de la création d'une instance de la classe primitive" is a calque of "primitive class": in French "classe primitive" reads as a *primitive/basic* class rather than "the primitive's class" — "la classe de la primitive" (or "de la classe de primitive") is what a native writer would put, especially since line 100 already uses the correct "La classe d'options de la primitive". (2) Line 125 splits the two link labels as "la [suppression] et la [mitigation des erreurs]", so the first link reads as bare "suppression" and only picks up "des erreurs" from the far end of the sentence; "la [suppression des erreurs] et la [mitigation des erreurs]" keeps both concepts self-contained. Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (primitive, dictionnaire, valeur par défaut, auto-complétion, mises à jour groupées; Estimator/Sampler/Executor and `Unset` kept in English, as they should be).

examples.source: When creating an instance of the primitive class, you can pass in an instance of the `options` class.
examples.suggested: Lors de la création d'une instance de la classe de la primitive, tu peux transmettre une instance de la classe `options`.
examples.translation: Lors de la création d'une instance de la classe primitive, tu peux transmettre une instance de la classe `options`.
examples.why: Calque of the English noun-adjunct "primitive class". In French, "la classe primitive" parses as an adjective (a primitive/elementary class), not as "the class of the primitive". The file itself uses the correct genitive form later (line 100: "La classe d'options de la primitive"), so this is also an internal inconsistency.

examples.source: Find details about how to configure [error suppression](...) and [error mitigation](...).
examples.suggested: Découvre comment configurer la [suppression des erreurs](error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques) et la [mitigation des erreurs](error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques).
examples.translation: Découvre comment configurer la [suppression](error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques) et la [mitigation des erreurs](error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques).
examples.why: The English has two fully-formed terms; the French leaves the first link labelled just "suppression", which only becomes "suppression des erreurs" by borrowing the tail of the second phrase. Link labels are read out of context (and by screen readers), so the first one should carry its own complement.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every negation, caveat and quantity survives intact (the bolded "__לא__ נכון ש..." keeps the English "It is __not__ the case that...", the discrete-log conjecture, the "no longer outperforms" clause and the 1.0 diagonal answer are all faithful), so nothing here misleads a learner — but a native technical editor would rewrite a lot. The file contains several non-words / wrong words that a Hebrew writer would never produce: "ברכיתן" (line 73, for "superficially", not a Hebrew word), "שייושנו" ("will be aged", line 113, where "שיידונו" = "will be discussed" is meant), "מונחות מפתח" (line 126, should be "מונחי מפתח"), "עיבוד לאחר" (line 166, a broken calque of "post-processing"), "הנחת החקירה" (line 77, "facilitating exploration" turned into "the laying-down of the exploration") and "אחד מתחומי הריגוש הרבים" (line 33, "areas of arousal" for "exciting areas"). Domain terms are imperfect but recognizable rather than false: "interference" → "הפרעה" (disturbance) instead of the standard physics term "התאבכות" (line 113), "diagonalization" → "אלכסון" instead of "ליכסון" (line 27), "rigorous" → "מחמיר" ("severe") in the Nature paper title (line 93). Terminology is also inconsistent: "circuit" is "מעגל קוונטי" throughout but suddenly "Circuit קוונטי" at line 286, and qubit alternates between "Qubit" (lines 32, 59) and lowercase "qubit" (line 73). Register holds informal ("תוכלו", "שימו לב", "ראו"), with one jussive slip ("אל יירתעו", line 157). Separately, structural, not prose: the first two check-in answers lost their Accordion wrapper (lines 111-119) so the answers render open, which weakens the self-check the English intends.

examples.source: There are many other differences that will be discussed in future lessons, including entanglement and interference.
examples.suggested: ישנם הבדלים רבים נוספים שיידונו בשיעורים עתידיים, כולל שזירה והתאבכות.
examples.translation: ישנם הבדלים רבים נוספים שייושנו בשיעורים עתידיים, כולל שזירה והפרעה.
examples.why: Two defects in one sentence: 'שייושנו' is not the verb for 'will be discussed' (it reads as 'will be aged/obsoleted'), and quantum interference is 'התאבכות' in Hebrew physics — 'הפרעה' means disturbance/noise, which points the learner at decoherence rather than at the interference of amplitudes.

examples.source: The above statements have been made very carefully such that they are true (many superficially similar statements are incorrect).
examples.suggested: האמירות לעיל נוסחו בזהירות רבה כך שהן נכונות (אמירות רבות הדומות להן למראית עין הן שגויות).
examples.translation: האמירות לעיל נוסחו בזהירות רבה כך שהן נכונות (אמירות רבות הדומות להן ברכיתן שגויות).
examples.why: 'ברכיתן' is not a Hebrew word at all; the qualifier 'superficially' — the whole point of the parenthesis — dissolves into noise, and the reader stumbles mid-sentence.

examples.source: One also sees the differences between complex and real coefficients emphasized, as in:
examples.suggested: אפשר גם למצוא הדגשה של ההבדלים בין מקדמים מרוכבים לממשיים, למשל:
examples.translation: גם ניתן לראות שהדגשים בין מקדמים מרוכבים לממשיים מודגשים, כמו:
examples.why: 'differences' became 'הדגשים' (emphases), producing the circular 'the emphases ... are emphasized'. The setup sentence for the real-vs-complex amplitude contrast no longer names the contrast it is introducing; only the following paragraph rescues it.

examples.source: So what we have done above is created a quantum circuit that contains the features of our two data points
examples.suggested: אז מה שעשינו לעיל הוא שיצרנו מעגל קוונטי המכיל את המאפיינים של שתי נקודות הנתונים שלנו
examples.translation: אז מה שעשינו לעיל הוא יצרנו Circuit קוונטי המכיל את המאפיינים של שתי נקודות הנתונים שלנו
examples.why: 'circuit' is rendered 'מעגל קוונטי' everywhere else in the file (lines 50, 51, 53, 77); leaving the bare English 'Circuit' here breaks the convention mid-file. Same split for qubit: 'Qubit' at lines 32/59 vs lowercase 'qubit' at line 73.

examples.source: A rigorous and robust quantum speed-up in supervised machine learning.
examples.suggested: האצה קוונטית קפדנית ועמידה בלמידת מכונה מפוקחת.
examples.translation: יתרון מהירות קוונטי מחמיר ואמין בלמידת מכונה מפוקחת.
examples.why: 'rigorous' rendered as 'מחמיר' means 'severe/stricter' — a speed-up cannot be 'severe' in Hebrew, and the cited paper title becomes unsearchable. 'קפדני'/'מוקפד' is the term for a rigorous result.

examples.source: Step 4: Analyzing / post-processing
examples.suggested: שלב 4: ניתוח / עיבוד בדיעבד
examples.translation: שלב 4: ניתוח / עיבוד לאחר
examples.why: 'עיבוד לאחר' is an incomplete calque — the preposition 'לאחר' dangles with no object. This is one of the four named Qiskit-patterns steps the course repeats throughout, so the broken label will be carried into later lessons.

editor_note: Meaning is preserved throughout and nothing here would teach a learner something false, but a native technical editor would rework several passages. The opening description renders "a post-processing step that measures…" as "שלב עיבוד לאחר שמודד…", where "לאחר ש-" is read in Hebrew as the conjunction "after [it] measures", garbling the syntax of the key procedural sentence (the three-step sequence still survives, so it confuses rather than misleads). "bitwise AND" is downgraded to "AND בוליאני" (boolean AND), and "fractional gates" is rendered "שערים שברים" (noun apposition; the adjectival "שערים שבריים" is what a Hebrew writer would use). Core terms are also split within the file — "circuit" appears both as "ה-Circuit" (lines 39, 95) and "מעגל" (33, 70, 241), and "spectator" both as "ספקטטור" (33) and "spectator" (126, 130) — plus a handful of noun-noun calques ("מידע qubit", "shot מדידה", "מידע קישוריות של שכן קרוב" for nearest-neighbor).

examples.source: One such method for doing so involves appending a circuit with a post-processing step that measures active and adjacent "spectator" qubits, applies a slow rotation to each qubit, and then measures them again.
examples.suggested: שיטה אחת לכך היא הוספה למעגל של שלב עיבוד-לאחר (post-processing) שמודד את ה-qubits הפעילים ואת ה-qubits ה"צופים" (spectator) הסמוכים, מפעיל סיבוב איטי על כל qubit, ומודד אותם שוב.
examples.translation: שיטה אחת לעשות זאת כוללת הוספת מעגל עם שלב עיבוד לאחר שמודד qubits פעילים וסמוכים "ספקטטור", מיישם סיבוב איטי על כל qubit, ולאחר מכן מודד אותם שוב.
examples.why: "שלב עיבוד לאחר ש..." is parsed by a Hebrew reader as the conjunction "after it measures", not as "post-processing step that measures". The core procedural sentence of the page becomes syntactically ambiguous, and "הוספת מעגל" also inverts what is appended to what.

examples.source: This notebook takes a bitwise AND, which is a conservative strategy that retains a shot only if it is passed by both node and edge strategies.
examples.suggested: ה-notebook הזה מבצע AND ביטווייז (bitwise), אסטרטגיה שמרנית ששומרת shot רק אם הוא עובר גם את אסטרטגיית ה-node וגם את זו של ה-edge.
examples.translation: ה-notebook הזה לוקח AND בוליאני, שהיא אסטרטגיה שמרנית שמשמרת shot רק אם הוא עובר גם אסטרטגיות ה-node וגם ה-edge.
examples.why: "bitwise" was replaced by "בוליאני" (boolean) — a different operator concept, even if the effect on a boolean mask array is the same here. Also "לוקח AND" is a literal calque of English "takes an AND".

examples.source: Start by preparing the circuit to execute and transpile against a backend that supports fractional gates.
examples.suggested: התחל בהכנת המעגל להרצה ובביצוע transpile מול Backend שתומך בשערים שבריים (fractional gates).
examples.translation: התחל בהכנת ה-Circuit להרצה ו-transpile אל Backend שתומך בשערים שברים.
examples.why: "שערים שברים" is a noun-noun apposition; the adjectival form is "שערים שבריים", and the current wording sits uncomfortably close to "שערים שבורים" (broken gates). This line also starts the circuit split: "ה-Circuit" here and in line 95 vs "מעגל" in lines 33, 70 and 241.

examples.source: The first strategy, `node`, uses qubit information to decide whether a measurement shot should be discarded — and the second, `edge`, uses nearest-neighbor connectivity information to make this decision.
examples.translation: האסטרטגיה הראשונה, `node`, משתמשת במידע qubit כדי להחליט האם shot מדידה צריך להיזרק — והשנייה, `edge`, משתמשת במידע קישוריות של שכן קרוב לקבל החלטה זו.
examples.why: Three English noun-noun compounds are carried over untranslated in structure: "מידע qubit" (should be "מידע ברמת ה-qubit"), "shot מדידה" (should be "shot של מדידה"), and "מידע קישוריות של שכן קרוב" (should be "מידע על קישוריות בין שכנים קרובים" — "nearest-neighbor" is a superlative that was flattened to "close neighbor"). Grammatical, but unmistakably translated rather than written.

examples.source: Next, create a preset pass manager that includes the AddPostSelectionMeasures and AddSpectatorMeasures passes
examples.suggested: לאחר מכן, צור pass manager מוגדר-מראש (preset) שכולל את ה-passes ...
examples.translation: לאחר מכן, צור pass manager מוכן שכולל את ה-passes ...
examples.why: "מוכן" means "ready", not "preset/predefined"; `preset pass manager` is a specific Qiskit construct (generate_preset_pass_manager) and the Hebrew loses that it refers to a predefined configuration.

editor_note: Nothing here teaches a false concept — core terminology is right and consistent (qubit, keunggulan kuantum / utilitas kuantum, entanglement, fault-tolerant, mitigasi kesalahan, sirkuit terpadu) and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout — but a native technical editor would rewrite a fair amount. Two glossary leaks survive as capitalized English mid-sentence: "Circuit kuantum" (line 81, while line 215 correctly says "sirkuit") and "Gate"/"fidelitas Gate 2 qubit" (lines 209, 217-219). English "matched" is rendered two ways: correctly as "tidak bisa ditandingi" (line 41) but as "dicocokkan" (line 55), which in Indonesian means "matched up / checked for agreement" rather than "equalled"; likewise "quantum mechanical systems" is "sistem mekanik kuantum" (lines 35, 45, 146-147, i.e. *mechanical* engineering) although the file uses the correct "Mekanika kuantum" at 138/140. Several sentences are raw calques a native writer would never produce — "Kita akan memiliki lebih banyak yang dikatakan tentang ini nanti!" (52), "Ini bukan lagi kasusnya." (175, vs. the natural "ini tidak lagi berlaku" at 63), "menarik fisika dan teknologi komputasi dengan cara bootstraps" (119, which breaks the analogy entirely), "keuntungan dari penglihatan ke belakang" (229) — plus a dropped referent at 149 and a reversed preposition at 135.

examples.source: assumes a basic familiarity with qubits and quantum circuits
examples.suggested: mengasumsikan pemahaman dasar tentang qubit dan sirkuit kuantum
examples.translation: mengasumsikan keakraban dasar dengan qubit dan Circuit kuantum
examples.why: Capitalized English "Circuit" is an untranslated glossary leak, and it contradicts the file's own "sirkuit qubit superkonduktor" (line 215). Same leak pattern for "Gate" at lines 209/217-219 ("Kualitas Gate", "fidelitas Gate 2 qubit").

examples.source: Its results can still be matched by advanced techniques running on classical computers
examples.suggested: Hasilnya masih bisa ditandingi oleh teknik canggih yang berjalan di komputer klasik
examples.translation: Hasilnya masih bisa dicocokkan oleh teknik canggih yang berjalan di komputer klasik
examples.why: "dicocokkan" means "matched up / cross-checked", not "equalled". Line 41 already renders the same English "matched" correctly as "tidak bisa ditandingi secara klasik", so the file is internally inconsistent on a load-bearing verb of the utility-vs-advantage argument.

examples.source: Instead we must look to the physical world for new computational tools
examples.suggested: Sebaliknya kita harus menengok ke dunia fisik untuk mencari alat komputasi baru
examples.translation: Sebaliknya kita harus mencari dunia fisik untuk alat komputasi baru
examples.why: "mencari dunia fisik" reads as "search FOR the physical world" — the preposition is inverted relative to "look TO the physical world". Line 91 handles the same idea correctly ("mencari bantuan dari dunia fisik").

examples.source: essentially pulling physics and computational technology up by the bootstraps
examples.suggested: pada dasarnya mengangkat fisika dan teknologi komputasi secara bersamaan, saling menopang satu sama lain
examples.translation: pada dasarnya menarik fisika dan teknologi komputasi dengan cara bootstraps
examples.why: "dengan cara bootstraps" is an untranslated English idiom that carries no meaning in Indonesian; the closing image of the section (physics and computing lifting each other) is lost, so the paragraph ends on an opaque phrase instead of the intuition the English builds.

examples.source: We'll have more to say about this later!
examples.suggested: Kita akan membahas ini lebih lanjut nanti!
examples.translation: Kita akan memiliki lebih banyak yang dikatakan tentang ini nanti!
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English "have ... to say" construction; no Indonesian technical writer would produce it. Compare the parallel line 178, "Kita akan merangkum ... dalam bagian di bawah ini", which is idiomatic. Line 175 "Ini bukan lagi kasusnya." ("No longer is this the case") is the same defect.

examples.source: Today this is one of the most promising avenues for quantum computing.
examples.suggested: Saat ini, hal ini merupakan salah satu jalan yang paling menjanjikan bagi komputasi kuantum.
examples.translation: Hari ini adalah salah satu jalan yang paling menjanjikan untuk komputasi kuantum.
examples.why: The subject "this" (simulating quantum systems, from the preceding paragraph) is dropped, so the sentence literally asserts that *today* is a promising avenue. The referent linking Feynman's proposal to the present-day case is lost.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner — the SABRE mechanics, the pm_1/pm_2/pm_3/pm_star comparison, all numbers, and the StarPreRouting caveats are transferred faithfully, and the informal "kamu" register holds throughout. But the file mixes an untranslated, mid-sentence-capitalized "Circuit" (frontmatter description, "Transpilasi mengubah Circuit kuantum…" ~L32, "setiap Circuit yang ditranspilasi" ~L390, ~L444) with "sirkuit" used dozens of times everywhere else — a glossary leak that should be unified to "sirkuit". Several passages are visible calques a native technical writer would rewrite: "Menggerbangkan `SabreLayout`" for "It gates SabreLayout" (~L159), "Keduanya datang dengan biaya waktu transpilasi yang lebih lama" (~L141), "preset default yang sebaliknya sama" for "an otherwise default preset" (~L536), "serupa semangatnya" for "similar in spirit" (~L538), "`basic` duduk jauh di bawah yang lain" (~L906), and "overhead distribusi biasanya mendominasi kecepatan apa pun" where EN says overhead dominates any *speedup* (~L911). Two small nuance losses: "a useful counter-example" flattened to "contoh yang berguna" (~L441, drops the counter- contrast that is the whole pedagogical point of the sentence), and `decay`'s "discouraging repeated swaps" strengthened to "mencegah swap berulang" (prevents), which overstates what a weighting heuristic does.

examples.source: Transpilation converts quantum circuits into forms compatible with…; We run each transpiled circuit 10 times…
examples.suggested: Transpilasi mengubah sirkuit kuantum…; setiap sirkuit yang ditranspilasi…
examples.translation: Transpilasi mengubah Circuit kuantum ke bentuk yang kompatibel…; Kita menjalankan setiap Circuit yang ditranspilasi 10 kali…
examples.why: Untranslated, capitalized "Circuit" (a glossary leak) sits alongside "sirkuit", which the rest of the file uses dozens of times — within-file inconsistency for the single most frequent domain term.

examples.source: It gates `SabreLayout` so it only runs when `VF2Layout` at [1] failed to find a perfect mapping
examples.suggested: Ia membatasi `SabreLayout` agar hanya berjalan ketika `VF2Layout` pada [1] gagal menemukan pemetaan sempurna
examples.translation: Menggerbangkan `SabreLayout` sehingga hanya berjalan ketika `VF2Layout` pada [1] gagal menemukan pemetaan sempurna
examples.why: "Menggerbangkan" is a literal coinage from the English verb "to gate" (gerbang = door/gate); no Indonesian technical writer would use it — it also collides with "gerbang" as the hardware gate.

examples.source: `pm_2` is a useful counter-example: although its 2Q depth is lower than `pm_1`'s, its mean fidelity ends up marginally lower as well
examples.suggested: `pm_2` adalah contoh penyangkal yang berguna: meskipun kedalaman 2Q-nya lebih rendah dari `pm_1`, …
examples.translation: `pm_2` adalah contoh yang berguna: meskipun kedalaman 2Q-nya lebih rendah dari `pm_1`, rata-rata fidelitasnya justru sedikit lebih rendah juga
examples.why: "counter-example" flattened to plain "contoh"; the paragraph's teaching point is that pm_2 runs *against* the depth→fidelity expectation, and that framing is lost in the topic sentence.

examples.source: **`decay`** (default): Dynamically weights qubits based on recent activity, discouraging repeated swaps on the same qubits.
examples.suggested: …, sehingga swap berulang pada qubit yang sama menjadi kurang disukai / dihambat.
examples.translation: **`decay`** (default): Memberikan bobot dinamis pada qubit berdasarkan aktivitas terkini, mencegah swap berulang pada qubit yang sama.
examples.why: "mencegah" means prevents; the heuristic only penalizes/discourages repeated swaps. Strengthens the claim from a soft weighting into a hard prohibition.

examples.source: Adds `StarPreRouting` to the init stage of an otherwise default preset.
examples.suggested: Menambahkan `StarPreRouting` ke tahap init dari preset yang selebihnya masih default.
examples.translation: Menambahkan `StarPreRouting` ke tahap init dari preset default yang sebaliknya sama.
examples.why: "yang sebaliknya sama" is a word-for-word rendering of "otherwise"; in Indonesian "sebaliknya" means "on the contrary", so the phrase reads as a contradiction rather than "in all other respects default".

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, the philosophical caveat on superposition and the "50%/100%" figures all survive intact, and the informal "tu" register holds consistently ("puoi", "pensalo", "ti abbiamo sfidato"). The defects are surface-level. (1) A glossary leak: "circuit" is left as capitalized English "Circuit" inside Italian prose six times (lines 47, 196, 334, 338, 344 twice — "stati e Circuit quantistici", "nel Circuit nella Lezione 1", "usando quel Circuit ... il tuo Circuit produce"), while the correct "circuito/circuiti" is used everywhere else (lines 25, 42, 197, 215, 344) — line 344 even mixes both in one sentence. Recognizable, so not misleading, but a native editor would fix all six. (2) Agreement slip at line 145: "Questo è chiamato la base computazionale" (masculine "chiamato" against feminine "base"); should be "Questa è chiamata base computazionale". (3) "collassa/collassano verso" (lines 141, 151-153, 329) is a calque of "collapses to"; Italian QM prose says "collassa in/su" (or "nello stato ..."). (4) "osservabile" is introduced correctly as a feminine noun ("qualsiasi grandezza misurabile è chiamata *osservabile*") then immediately taken as masculine in the same sentence ("gli osservabili sono rappresentati da matrici", line 184).

examples.source: a common language in which to discuss quantum states and circuits / confirm that your circuit produces the desired state
examples.suggested: ...di stati e circuiti quantistici / ...che il tuo circuito produce lo stato desiderato
examples.translation: un linguaggio comune per discutere di stati e Circuit quantistici / conferma che il tuo Circuit produce lo stato desiderato
examples.why: Untranslated capitalized English "Circuit" leaks into Italian prose six times while "circuito/circuiti" is used correctly elsewhere in the same file (line 344 mixes both within one sentence). Recognizable, so not misleading, but it is a clear within-file inconsistency and a glossary-protection artifact.

examples.source: This is called the computational basis, or $Z$ basis, which is defined by the states...
examples.suggested: Questa è chiamata base computazionale, o base $Z$, definita dagli stati...
examples.translation: Questo è chiamato la base computazionale, o base $Z$, definita dagli stati...
examples.why: Gender/number agreement failure ('chiamato' masculine against feminine 'base'), a calque of the English 'This is called the...' construction that no Italian technical writer would produce.

examples.source: the qubit collapses to the observed outcome / measurement outcomes collapse to |0> or |1>
examples.suggested: il qubit collassa nell'esito osservato / la misurazione collassa nello stato $\vert 0\rangle$ o $\vert 1\rangle$
examples.translation: il qubit collassa verso l'esito osservato / gli esiti ... collassano verso $\vert 0\rangle$ o $\vert 1\rangle$
examples.why: 'collassare verso' is a literal rendering of 'collapse to' and reads as translationese; standard Italian QM usage is 'collassare in/su' (collapse into a state). Consistent but consistently calqued.

examples.source: any measurable quantity is called an *observable*, and observables are represented by matrices
examples.suggested: ...è chiamata *osservabile*, e le osservabili sono rappresentate da matrici
examples.translation: qualsiasi grandezza misurabile è chiamata *osservabile*, e gli osservabili sono rappresentati da matrici
examples.why: The noun 'osservabile' is feminine in Italian physics usage and is introduced as such in the first half of the sentence, then flips to masculine ('gli osservabili sono rappresentati') in the second half — an internal gender inconsistency inside a single sentence.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: the table cells, the support key ("Supporto parziale"/"Non supportato") and all nine notes match the English claim-for-claim, terminology is correct and consistent (qubit → qubit, transpiled → "transpilato"/"transpilati", backend/ISA/runtime/box kept in English, "Ridotti a costanti nei parametri di gate" for constant-folded), and the informal register holds throughout ("consulta", "puoi usare tranquillamente", "Scopri", "Verifica il tuo programma"). What a native technical editor would still change is a handful of English-shaped sentences in the Admonition and in notes 1 and 7: "Questo esclude le definizioni di `gate` personalizzate ... dall'essere validi ... così come sono" is a word-for-word calque of "precludes ... from being valid ... verbatim"; "funzionalità che non possono essere caricate da Qiskit SDK da OpenQASM 3" stacks two "da" on different roles (agent vs. source); "Per i circuiti costruiti e inviati in questo modo non è necessario caricarli" left-dislocates with a resumptive pronoun where a plain subject sentence is idiomatic. One wording is mildly ambiguous rather than wrong: "l'analisi di espressioni variabili" reads as "expressions that vary" instead of "expressions over variables" (EN "variable expressions", in context of `expr.Var`).

examples.source: This precludes custom `gate` definitions and higher-level constructs like gate modifiers (such as `inv @`) from being valid for execution on hardware verbatim, but the `transpile` process resolves them into valid ISA circuits.
examples.suggested: Ciò impedisce che le definizioni di `gate` personalizzate e i costrutti di livello superiore come i modificatori di gate (per esempio `inv @`) siano validi per l'esecuzione sull'hardware nella loro forma originale, ma il processo di `transpile` li risolve in circuiti ISA validi.
examples.translation: Questo esclude le definizioni di `gate` personalizzate e i costrutti di livello superiore come i modificatori di gate (come `inv @`) dall'essere validi per l'esecuzione sull'hardware così come sono, ma il processo di `transpile` li risolve in circuiti ISA validi.
examples.why: "esclude ... dall'essere validi" is a literal transposition of "precludes ... from being valid"; Italian expresses this with "impedire che + congiuntivo". Meaning is preserved, but the sentence reads as machine-shaped.

examples.source: This includes features that cannot be loaded by Qiskit SDK from OpenQASM 3.
examples.suggested: Sono incluse anche le funzionalità che Qiskit SDK non è in grado di caricare da OpenQASM 3.
examples.translation: Questo include funzionalità che non possono essere caricate da Qiskit SDK da OpenQASM 3.
examples.why: Two consecutive "da" carrying different functions (agent, then source) makes the sentence momentarily unparsable; an active clause removes the collision.

examples.source: Circuits constructed and submitted in this manner do not need to be loaded from OpenQASM 3 files into Qiskit SDK.
examples.suggested: I circuiti costruiti e inviati in questo modo non devono essere caricati in Qiskit SDK da file OpenQASM 3.
examples.translation: Per i circuiti costruiti e inviati in questo modo non è necessario caricarli da file OpenQASM 3 in Qiskit SDK.
examples.why: The "Per i circuiti ... caricarli" dislocation with a resumptive pronoun is spoken-register and clumsy in technical prose; the plain passive is what a native writer would use.

examples.source: ...and has very limited support for parsing variable expressions.
examples.suggested: ...e ha un supporto molto limitato per l'analisi di espressioni contenenti variabili.
examples.translation: ...e ha un supporto molto limitato per l'analisi di espressioni variabili.
examples.why: "espressioni variabili" reads as "expressions that vary" (adjective) rather than "expressions over variables", which is what the note means in context of `expr.Var` declarations.

examples.source: ...backend execution always requires circuits to have been compiled to the backend Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), where `include` files are irrelevant.
examples.suggested: ...l'esecuzione sul backend richiede sempre che i circuiti siano stati compilati per l'Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) del backend, contesto in cui i file `include` non hanno alcuna rilevanza.
examples.translation: ...l'esecuzione sul backend richiede sempre che i circuiti siano stati compilati per l'Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) del backend, dove i file `include` non sono rilevanti.
examples.why: Locative "dove" calques English "where" used in the abstract sense; in Italian it briefly suggests a place, i.e. the ISA itself, rather than the situation described.

editor_note: Terminology is solid and consistent (qubit/Circuit/Gate kept in English per project convention; コヒーレンス時間・位相緩和時間 for T1/T2, エラー訂正/エラー緩和, ハミルトニアン・シミュレーション, 変分アルゴリズム, 偏微分方程式, 量子カーネル all correct), register is plain desu/masu with no keigo, and nothing teaches a false concept. What a native editor would change: one raw English word is left untranslated mid-sentence ("量子系は古典コンピューターでシミュレートするのが notoriously 困難です"); the opening "There is no doubt that there is a lot of excitement…" is re-scoped so 疑いの余地がありません now attaches to the technology's possibilities rather than to the excitement, strengthening the claim in a paragraph whose whole point is that hype makes fact hard to separate from fiction; the quantity-vs-quality sentence ("数量のスケールアップは確かに重要な要素ですが、qubit 自体の品質と同様に重要です") uses a concessive が against a same-subject clause, flattening the English emphasis that quality matters no less than quantity; and the conclusion calques "isn't about X, it's about Y" as 「〜についてではない…〜についてです」, which no Japanese technical writer would produce. Smaller items: 普遍性 for "ubiquity" (should be 遍在性), the unpunctuated 計算上手に負えなく, and the dropped "Hopefully".

examples.source: quantum systems are notoriously difficult to simulate on classical computers
examples.suggested: 量子系は古典コンピューターでシミュレートするのが非常に困難なことで知られています。
examples.translation: 量子系は古典コンピューターでシミュレートするのが notoriously 困難です。
examples.why: An untranslated English adverb is left embedded in the Japanese sentence — a raw source leak that stops the reader cold; the idiom needs 〜ことで知られています, not a transliterated word.

examples.source: There is no doubt that there is a lot of excitement about quantum computing, and the possibilities this technology could offer.
examples.suggested: 量子コンピューティングと、この技術がもたらしうる可能性に大きな期待が寄せられていることは間違いありません。
examples.translation: 量子コンピューティングには多くの興奮があり、この技術が提供しうる可能性については疑いの余地がありません。
examples.why: The English puts 'no doubt' on the existence of the excitement; the Japanese re-scopes it onto the possibilities themselves, so the text now asserts the technology's potential is beyond dispute — a strengthened claim in the very paragraph that goes on to warn that hype makes fact hard to tell from fiction.

examples.source: While scaling up in quantity is certainly a crucial element, it is no more important than quality of the qubits themselves.
examples.suggested: 数量のスケールアップは確かに重要な要素ですが、qubit 自体の品質もそれに劣らず重要です。
examples.translation: 数量のスケールアップは確かに重要な要素ですが、qubit 自体の品質と同様に重要です。
examples.why: The concessive が sets up a contrast and then the clause keeps the same subject (quantity), so the sentence reads as 'quantity is important, but quantity is equally important'. The English point — that quality is no less important than quantity — is the lesson's actual teaching beat and gets blurred.

examples.source: quantum advantage isn't about replacing computers. It's about expanding what's computable.
examples.suggested: 量子優位とは、コンピューターを置き換えることではなく、計算可能な範囲を広げることです。
examples.translation: 量子優位はコンピューターを置き換えることについてではないことが明らかになりました。計算可能なものを拡張することについてです。
examples.why: Direct calque of the English 'is about X' construction; 〜についてではない／〜についてです is not idiomatic Japanese and makes the lesson's punchline read as machine output rather than a written conclusion.

examples.source: optimization remains a major area of interest due to its ubiquity
examples.suggested: 最適化問題があらゆる分野に遍在することと、最適化の目的関数と量子ハミルトニアンの自然な対応関係から、最適化は主要な関心領域であり続けます
examples.translation: その普遍性と最適化目的と量子ハミルトニアンの自然なマッピングから、最適化は主要な関心領域であり続けます
examples.why: 'Ubiquity' (problems appear everywhere) is rendered as 普遍性 (universality), a different concept; the sentence also chains three と particles, making the two reasons hard to parse.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, and the tricky spots are handled correctly ("only if its corresponding control bit is |1⟩" → 「対応する制御ビットが $|1\rangle$ のときにのみ」, the run-on 「$U$ はユニタリであるため、その固有値はすべてノルムが 1 です」 split cleanly). What a native technical editor would change is within-file terminology consistency: "circuit" appears as bare capitalized 「Circuit」 in §2.4 (heading 「3 qubit QFT の Circuit 構成」, 「QFT Circuit をどのように構成するか」, 「状態 5 を符号化する Circuit を作成します」) but as 回路 in §4 and line 490 — 回路 is the standard term and the raw English word reads like an untranslated leak. "qubit" is likewise left in English through §1–§2 (「$N$ qubit」, 「4 つの qubit」, once capitalized as 「4 つの Qubit」 in the video title) but switches to 量子ビット throughout §3–§4. Smaller splits: 「Qiskit パターンズフレームワーク」 (ja:160) vs 「Qiskit パターン」 (ja:552), 「Shor のアルゴリズム」 (ja:34) vs 「ショアのアルゴリズム」 (ja:490), and 「Aer シミュレータ」 (ja:225) vs 「Aer シミュレーター」 (ja:466). Register is correct informal desu/masu with no keigo.

examples.source: ### 2.4 Example: Circuit construction of 3 qubits QFT / it might not be clear how to construct a QFT circuit
examples.suggested: ### 2.4 例：3 qubit QFT の回路構成 / QFT 回路をどのように構成するかは明確でないかもしれません
examples.translation: ### 2.4 例：3 qubit QFT の Circuit 構成 / QFT Circuit をどのように構成するかは明確でないかもしれません
examples.why: "circuit" is left as the bare English word 「Circuit」 in §2.4 (four occurrences) but correctly rendered 回路 in §4 (「回路を最適化する」「ターゲット回路」) and at ja:490. 回路 is the settled Japanese term; the capitalized English word inside Japanese prose reads as an untranslated leak, and the split is inconsistent within one file.

examples.source: qubit / counting qubits / 3 qubits for counting
examples.suggested: Pick one convention for the whole file — either qubit throughout or 量子ビット throughout (量子ビット is the more common choice in Japanese Qiskit material).
examples.translation: 「$N$ qubit に対して」「4 つの qubit を使って」 … vs 「追加の $n$ 量子ビットからなる」「カウンティング量子ビットに」「3 量子ビットのカウンティング」
examples.why: The core term is rendered in English in sections 1–2 and in Japanese in sections 3–4. The concept stays identifiable, so this is not misleading, but a native editor would unify it; the video title at ja:80 additionally capitalizes it as 「4 つの Qubit」.

examples.source: we will not use the Qiskit patterns framework … follow 4 steps of Qiskit patterns
examples.suggested: Use 「Qiskit パターン」 in both places (or keep "Qiskit patterns" in English in both).
examples.translation: 「Qiskit パターンズフレームワークを使用しません」 … 「Qiskit パターンの 4 ステップに従います」
examples.why: Same product concept named two ways in one file; 「パターンズ」 is an unusual transliteration that a Japanese reader may not immediately connect to the 「Qiskit パターン」 used 400 lines later.

examples.source: Shor's algorithm allows us to factorize a number by building a circuit with θ unknown and obtaining θ. / Estimate θ = 1/3 using 3 qubits for counting and a qubit for an eigenvector.
examples.suggested: 「$\theta$ を未知数とした回路を構築し、その $\theta$ を求めることで…」 / 「カウンティング用の 3 量子ビットと固有ベクトル用の 1 量子ビットを使って…」
examples.translation: 「ショアのアルゴリズムでは、$\theta$ を未知としてその値を回路から取得することで、数の素因数分解が可能になります。」 / 「3 量子ビットのカウンティングと固有ベクトル用の 1 量子ビットを使って、$\theta = 1/3$ を推定してください。」
examples.why: The first sentence flattens the English's two-step recipe (build a circuit with θ unknown, then obtain θ) into a single vague 「回路から取得する」, and uses ショア where ja:34 wrote 「Shor のアルゴリズム」. The second calques the English noun order into 「3 量子ビットのカウンティング」, which reads as "a counting of 3 qubits" rather than "3 counting qubits".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, and the SQD/configuration-recovery explanation (line 49–53) tracks the English closely — so nothing here misleads a learner. What a Korean technical editor would change: (1) "orbital" is consistently rendered as bare 궤도 ("궤도 점유율", "궤도 회전", "공간 궤도"), which reads as the classical *orbit*; Korean quantum-chemistry writing uses 오비탈 (공간 오비탈, 오비탈 회전) or 궤도함수. (2) Line 43 injects a gloss the English does not have: "1체 및 2체 전자 적분(각각 1전자/2전자 적분)" — factually correct, but added content. (3) "qubit" is spelled inconsistently within one sentence at line 125 ("qubit 상호 작용" vs "궤도(Qubit으로 표현)"), also 169 ("물리적 qubit") vs 159 ("127-Qubit"). (4) A few calqued spots: "우리 해에서 처음 다섯 개의 궤도를" (line 307) and "Circuit에 패스 매니저를 실행합니다" (line 172) are word-order transfers a native writer would recast (e.g. "우리가 얻은 해에서는…", "회로에 대해 패스 매니저를 실행합니다"). Register (합니다체 + -하세요) is the standard doc convention and holds; no honorific/humble slips.

examples.source: the average occupancy of each spatial orbital / decompose gates into orbital rotations / orbitals (represented by qubits)
examples.suggested: 각 공간 오비탈의 평균 점유율 / 게이트를 오비탈 회전으로 분해 / 오비탈(Qubit으로 표현)
examples.translation: 각 공간 궤도의 평균 점유율 / Gate를 궤도 회전으로 분해 / 궤도(Qubit으로 표현)
examples.why: Bare 궤도 is the word for a classical orbit; Korean quantum-chemistry convention for 'orbital' is 오비탈 (or 궤도함수). Recognizable in context, so not misleading, but it is the wrong domain term and it repeats file-wide (궤도 점유율, 궤도 회전, 공간 궤도).

examples.source: $h_{pr}$ and $(pr|qs)$ are the one- and two-body electronic integrals.
examples.suggested: $h_{pr}$과 $(pr|qs)$는 각각 1체 및 2체 전자 적분입니다.
examples.translation: $h_{pr}$과 $(pr|qs)$는 1체 및 2체 전자 적분(각각 1전자/2전자 적분)입니다.
examples.why: The parenthetical '(각각 1전자/2전자 적분)' has no counterpart in the English. It happens to be accurate, so it does not mislead, but the translation should not add explanatory glosses the source author did not write.

examples.source: qubit / 127-qubit backend / physical qubits
examples.suggested: Pick one casing for the kept-English term (e.g. always 'qubit') and apply it throughout.
examples.translation: qubit 상호 작용 … 궤도(Qubit으로 표현) / 가상 127-Qubit Backend / 물리적 qubit(`initial_layout`)
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: lowercase 'qubit' and capitalized 'Qubit' alternate, twice inside the same sentence at line 125. The concept stays identifiable, so this is cosmetic, but a native editor would normalize it.

examples.source: both the spin-up and spin-down electrons occupy the first five orbitals with high probability in our solutions. / Run the pass manager on your circuit.
examples.suggested: 우리가 얻은 해에서는 스핀업 전자와 스핀다운 전자가 모두 처음 다섯 개의 오비탈을 높은 확률로 점유하는 것을 볼 수 있습니다. / 회로에 대해 패스 매니저를 실행합니다.
examples.translation: 스핀업과 스핀다운 전자 모두 우리 해에서 처음 다섯 개의 궤도를 높은 확률로 점유하는 것을 볼 수 있습니다. / Circuit에 패스 매니저를 실행합니다.
examples.why: '우리 해에서' is a bare calque of 'in our solutions' and sits mid-clause where Korean would front it as a topic; 'Circuit에 …을 실행합니다' transfers English 'run X on Y' where Korean takes '…에 대해 실행합니다'. Grammatical but audibly translated.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no inverted conditions, no dropped caveats; the PNA definition (노이즈 채널의 역(inverse)을 통해 Observable을 전파), the non-monotonicity caveat on max_err_terms/max_obs_terms (단조 증가를 보장하지는 않습니다), and the num_to_measure explanation all match the English. What a native technical editor would change is consistency: "circuit" alternates between untranslated "Circuit" (Trotterized 양자 Circuit, Circuit을 Backend에 트랜스파일, Circuit 박스) and 회로 (회로 내 얽힘 게이트, 박스 처리된 회로), roughly split down the middle of the file; "qubit" appears three ways in adjacent bullets — "qubit 체인", "단일 큐비트 게이트", "모든 활성 Qubit"; "post-selection" is 사후 선택 everywhere except 포스트 선택(post-selected) in the post-processing section; and "canonical" is 표준 형태 in the heading but 정규 형식 / 정규 큐비트 순서 two lines later. Also "readout errors" is rendered literally as 읽기 오류 (conventional: 판독 오류 / 측정 오류), and the whole file is written in 합니다체 rather than the 해요체 house convention — though it matches its sibling qiskit-addons KO files (obp, cutting), so that is a subtree-wide convention split rather than a per-file slip. Nothing here would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Create a Trotterized quantum circuit and observable. / Before we learn the noise, we need to find the unique 2-qubit layers in our circuit
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering of "circuit" — 회로 (with Circuit only inside code identifiers) — and apply it to headings and body alike.
examples.translation: Trotterized 양자 Circuit과 Observable 생성 … / 노이즈를 학습하기 전에, 회로 내 고유한 2-큐비트 레이어를 찾아야 합니다.
examples.why: The same core term is untranslated "Circuit" in the first half of the file and 회로 in the second half, including in section headings ("Circuit 박스를 학습된 노이즈와 연결" vs "회로 끝까지 전파"). Recognizable, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: a chain of qubits on ibm_kingston / Single qubit gates will be left-dressed / Twirl all active qubits in each box
examples.suggested: 큐비트 throughout (큐비트 체인 / 단일 큐비트 게이트 / 모든 활성 큐비트).
examples.translation: ``ibm_kingston``에서 낮은 오류율을 보고하는 qubit 체인 / 단일 큐비트 게이트는 … / 얽힘 게이트를 포함하는 각 박스 내의 모든 활성 Qubit을 트와일링합니다
examples.why: "qubit" is rendered three different ways — bare English "qubit", capitalized "Qubit", and 큐비트 — within a handful of lines. The concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency defect, not a misleading one.

examples.source: Generate a mask for keeping only post-selected samples
examples.suggested: 사후 선택된 샘플만 유지하기 위한 마스크 생성
examples.translation: 포스트 선택(post-selected) 샘플만 유지하기 위한 마스크 생성
examples.why: The file establishes 사후 선택(post-selection) in the intro, the samplex section and the noise-learning bullets, then switches to the transliteration 포스트 선택 in the final post-processing list — the reader has to re-map an already-introduced term.

examples.source: Transform the measurement bases to canonical form / map these Pauli terms to the canonical form expected by the Executor primitive … canonical qubit ordering
examples.suggested: Use 정규 형식 in the heading too (측정 기저를 정규 형식으로 변환), matching the body.
examples.translation: 측정 기저를 표준 형태로 변환 … ``Executor`` 프리미티브가 기대하는 정규 형식(canonical form)으로 매핑해야 합니다 … 정규 큐비트 순서
examples.why: The heading's 표준 형태 and the body's 정규 형식 are the same English term two lines apart, which reads as if the heading and the paragraph describe different transformations.

examples.source: We will also use TREX to mitigate readout errors
examples.suggested: 또한 TREX를 사용하여 판독(readout) 오류를 완화하고
examples.translation: 또한 TREX를 사용하여 읽기 오류를 완화하고
examples.why: 읽기 오류 is a literal "read error" and in Korean IT prose more readily suggests a file/disk read failure; the established quantum term is 판독 오류 (or 측정 오류 / readout 오류). Recognizable in context, so minor.

examples.source: In this tutorial, we will learn how to leverage the latest tools … executing the experiment is straightforward.
examples.suggested: 배워요 / 간단해요 … if the 해요체 house convention is to apply to the qiskit-addons subtree as it does to guides/.
examples.translation: 이 튜토리얼에서는 … 구현하는 방법을 배웁니다. … 실험 실행은 간단합니다.
examples.why: The file is uniformly 합니다체 (34 instances, zero 해요) while the ko guides/ corpus is uniformly 해요체 (3,000+ instances). It matches its sibling addon files (obp, cutting), so it is internally and locally consistent — flagged only as the subtree-level register split, not as a per-file error.

editor_note: The core operation of the algorithm is taught wrongly: "diagonalization/diagonalize" is rendered throughout as "penjajaran / jajarkan / menjajari", which in Malay means alignment (menjajarkan = to align/make parallel), not matrix diagonalization (pemepenjuruan / pendiagonalan). This makes SQD read as "sample-based quantum alignment", and Step 4 reads "Unjur dan jajarkan Hamiltonian … ke atas setiap subruang" ("project and align the Hamiltonian"), so a learner forms a false belief about what SQD actually does — the same class of error as rendering "variational" as "permutational". Two further false-friend terms compound it: "7 bath sites" becomes "``7`` tapak mandi" (literally "bathing/shower places" instead of a bath/reservoir of sites, i.e. tapak mandian/takungan), and "quantum noise" becomes "bunyi kuantum" ("quantum sound") although the correct-sense word "bising" is used two sentences later for "noisy samples". Separately, "keadaan asas" is made to carry both "ground state" and "basis state", so "Jana satu set keadaan asas Krylov … untuk menganggar keadaan asas" uses one phrase for two different concepts in a single line; minor items are the ungrammatical "kejarangannya keadaan asas" (stray -nya), image alt text "Rajah Circuit kuantum" leaving "Circuit" in English while "litar" is used everywhere else, and mid-sentence capitalisation of "Backend"/"Qubit".

examples.source: We will follow a sample-based quantum diagonalization approach … Project and diagonalize the Fermionic lattice Hamiltonian over each sampled subspace … By the last iteration, we are diagonalizing in the entire Hilbert space.
examples.suggested: …pendekatan pemepenjuruan (pendiagonalan) kuantum berasaskan sampel … Unjur dan pepenjurukan Hamiltonian kekisi Fermionic ke atas setiap subruang yang disampel … kita sedang melakukan pemepenjuruan dalam keseluruhan ruang Hilbert.
examples.translation: Kita akan mengikuti pendekatan penjajaran kuantum berasaskan sampel … Unjur dan jajarkan Hamiltonian kekisi Fermionic ke atas setiap subruang yang disampel … Pada lelaran terakhir, kita sedang menjajari dalam keseluruhan ruang Hilbert.
examples.why: 'Menjajarkan' means to align/line up, a different mathematical operation entirely. Used consistently for every occurrence of 'diagonalize', it teaches the learner that SQD aligns rather than diagonalizes the Hamiltonian in each sampled subspace — a false concept about the algorithm's defining step.

examples.source: the one-dimensional single-impurity Anderson model (SIAM) with ``7`` bath sites (``8`` electrons in ``8`` orbitals)
examples.suggested: …dengan ``7`` tapak mandian (bath) (``8`` elektron dalam ``8`` orbital)
examples.translation: model Anderson single-impurity (SIAM) satu dimensi dengan ``7`` tapak mandi (``8`` elektron dalam ``8`` orbital)
examples.why: 'Tapak mandi' is a place for bathing/showering. The physics sense of 'bath' (a reservoir of non-interacting sites hybridised with the impurity) is lost, and the learner is handed a nonsensical picture of the SIAM lattice.

examples.source: In order to account for the effect of quantum noise, the configuration recovery technique is used.
examples.suggested: Bagi mengambil kira kesan hingar kuantum, teknik pemulihan konfigurasi digunakan.
examples.translation: Bagi mengambil kira kesan bunyi kuantum, teknik pemulihan konfigurasi digunakan.
examples.why: 'Bunyi' is acoustic sound; the signal-processing sense is 'hingar' (or at least 'bising', which this same file uses correctly for 'noisy samples' at line 161). As written it reads as 'the effect of quantum sound', and the term is split two ways within the file.

examples.source: a set of ``16``-qubit Krylov basis states … find an approximation to the ground state … combine the counts from each of the Krylov basis states
examples.suggested: satu set keadaan basis Krylov ``16``-qubit … mencari penghampiran kepada keadaan dasar/asas …
examples.translation: satu set keadaan asas Krylov ``16``-Qubit … mencari penghampiran kepada keadaan asas … kiraan daripada setiap keadaan asas Krylov
examples.why: 'Keadaan asas' is used for both 'basis state' and 'ground state'. In 'Jana satu set keadaan asas Krylov … untuk menganggar keadaan asas' (line 18) the identical phrase carries two different meanings in one sentence, so the reader cannot tell the Krylov subspace basis from the target ground state.

examples.source: Assuming a good initial state and sparsity of the ground state, this approach is proven to converge efficiently.
examples.suggested: Dengan mengandaikan keadaan awal yang baik dan kejarangan keadaan dasar, pendekatan ini terbukti menumpu dengan cekap.
examples.translation: Dengan mengandaikan keadaan awal yang baik dan kejarangannya keadaan asas, pendekatan ini terbukti menumpu dengan cekap.
examples.why: The possessive suffix -nya on 'kejarangannya' is ungrammatical before a following noun phrase; a native technical writer would write 'kejarangan keadaan dasar'.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: every prose sentence tracks the English faithfully, section headings and the Admonition list are semantically correct, and no caveat or quantity is dropped. The changes a native editor would make are surface-level. (1) "circuit" is left as the English word with a capital C inside running Malay throughout — "output Circuit kuantum", "bagi satu Circuit", "Jalankan Circuit berparameter", "kebolehgunaan semula Circuit", "prestasi Circuit pada QPU" — where Malay has the firmly established "litar (kuantum)"; it is consistent, so recognizable, but reads as a glossary keep-English artifact rather than something a Malay quantum engineer would write. (2) "error-mitigated" becomes "terurangan ralat", a non-standard morphological coinage; "dengan mitigasi ralat" or "yang diringankan ralatnya" is the natural rendering. (3) "measurement outcome" is rendered "hasil ukuran" (ukuran = size/measure) rather than the correct nominalization "hasil/keputusan pengukuran". (4) A register slip in the package-versions block: "Kami syorkan menggunakan…" should be "Kami mengesyorkan…"; likewise "disampel dari output" should be "daripada".

examples.source: Generate entire error-mitigated quasi-probability distributions sampled from quantum circuit outputs. / Run parameterized circuits
examples.suggested: …yang disampel daripada output litar kuantum. / Jalankan litar berparameter
examples.translation: Jana keseluruhan taburan quasi-kebarangkalian terurangan ralat yang disampel dari output Circuit kuantum. / Jalankan Circuit berparameter
examples.why: "Circuit" is kept in English (and capitalized mid-sentence) in all six prose occurrences. Malay has the standard, universally used domain term "litar kuantum"; this is not a term the field keeps in English in Malay, so the effect is translationese rather than a defensible loanword choice. Consistent, so not misleading — MINOR.

examples.source: error-mitigated quasi-probability distributions
examples.suggested: taburan kuasi-kebarangkalian dengan mitigasi ralat
examples.translation: taburan quasi-kebarangkalian terurangan ralat
examples.why: "terurangan" is not a well-formed Malay derivation (the productive forms are "dikurangkan"/"pengurangan"), and the noun-stacking "quasi-kebarangkalian terurangan ralat" is hard to parse. Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: Use Sampler to return the measurement outcome as bitstrings or counts of a single circuit.
examples.suggested: …untuk mengembalikan hasil pengukuran sebagai bitstring atau kiraan bagi satu litar.
examples.translation: Gunakan Sampler untuk mengembalikan hasil ukuran sebagai bitstring atau kiraan bagi satu Circuit.
examples.why: "ukuran" means size/dimension; the measurement process is "pengukuran". Used the same way in both section intros, so it is consistent but consistently the weaker term. "bitstring" and "kiraan" (counts) are correct.

examples.source: We recommend using these versions or newer.
examples.suggested: Kami mengesyorkan penggunaan versi ini atau yang lebih baru.
examples.translation: Kami syorkan menggunakan versi ini atau yang lebih baru.
examples.why: Bare-stem "syorkan" after a subject is colloquial; documentation register takes the meN- prefix. Same class of slip as "disampel dari" for "disampel daripada" in the intro line.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, swapped quantities or dropped caveats — and the informal "ty" register holds ("Zwróć uwagę", "Jeśli ta konwencja ci nie odpowiada", "Przypomnij sobie"), so nothing here misleads a learner. What a Polish editor would fix is a cluster of untranslated/uninflected English glossary leaks: "circuit" is rendered as bare capitalized "Circuit" in at least five places ("w postaci Circuit kwantowego", "listę Circuit", "Poniższy Circuit efektywnie mierzy Z", "Schemat Circuit pokazujący pomiar") while the very same term appears correctly as "obwodów" at line 439; "qubit" is capitalized mid-sentence as "Qubitu / Qubitów / Qubity" instead of lowercase "kubit"; and "eigenstate" survives as the non-word hybrid "eigenstanów" / "w eigenstate operatora x" (lines 292, 295) even though "stany własne" is used correctly everywhere else. The ΔS quantity is also split between "niepewność" and "nieoznaczoność" within the file (e.g. "iloczynu niepewności" line 607 vs "iloczyn nieoznaczoności" line 777), and two noun forms of "rzut" are garbled: "dodatnią i ujemną rzutnię na oś y" (line 605) and "ma większą rzutową na stany własne Y" (line 779). Smaller polish items: "kula Blocha" should be "sfera Blocha", "a i b są remisem" is a calque of "are tied", "Do zbierania statystyk pomiarów możemy użyć Sampler" needs the genitive "Samplera", and the heading "Check your understanding" alternates between "Sprawdź swoje rozumienie" and "Sprawdź swoją wiedzę" while "Krok 4: Post-processing" keeps the English noun despite "Przetwarzanie końcowe" being used in the step list.

examples.source: the mapping step is simply expressing the measurements and rotations described above in a quantum circuit / The circuit below effectively measures Z and then X
examples.suggested: w postaci obwodu kwantowego / Poniższy obwód efektywnie mierzy Z, a następnie X
examples.translation: sprowadza się do wyrażenia opisanych powyżej pomiarów i rotacji w postaci Circuit kwantowego / Poniższy Circuit efektywnie mierzy $Z$, a następnie $X$
examples.why: "circuit" is left as an uninflected capitalized English noun in at least five places (also "listę Circuit", "Schemat Circuit pokazujący pomiar"), which is ungrammatical in Polish next to the inflected adjective "kwantowego" — and the same term is correctly rendered "obwodów" at line 439, so the file contradicts itself.

examples.source: The measurement along x collapses the state into either an eigenstate |+>_x or the eigenstate |->_x … So once the system is in an eigenstate of x
examples.suggested: rzutuje stan na jeden ze stanów własnych … Skoro układ znalazł się w stanie własnym operatora $x$
examples.translation: Pomiar wzdłuż $x$ rzutuje stan na jeden z eigenstanów: $|+\rangle_x$ lub $|-\rangle_x$ … Skoro układ znalazł się w eigenstate operatora $x$
examples.why: "eigenstanów" and "w eigenstate" are English-Polish hybrids that are not Polish words; the file itself uses the correct "stany własne" everywhere else (lines 599, 602, 657), so this is an internal split of a core term.

examples.source: for a qubit or spin-1/2 particle … Qiskit orders qubits, measurements, and other things
examples.suggested: dla kubitu lub cząstki o spinie 1/2 … Qiskit porządkuje kubity, pomiary i inne elementy
examples.translation: dla Qubitu lub cząstki spin-1/2 … Qiskit porządkuje Qubity, pomiary i inne elementy
examples.why: Capitalizing "Qubit" mid-sentence is an artifact of glossary handling, not Polish orthography; Polish technical writing uses lowercase "kubit" (or lowercase "qubit"), and the capital marks the text as machine-processed.

examples.source: yield a positive projection on the y axis just as often as a negative projection … a quantum state that has a larger projection on eigenstates of Y
examples.suggested: dają dodatni rzut na oś $y$ równie często jak ujemny … stanu kwantowego, który ma większy rzut na stany własne $Y$
examples.translation: dają dodatnią i ujemną rzutnię na oś $y$ … stanu kwantowego, który ma większą rzutową na stany własne $Y$
examples.why: "rzutnia" means a projection plane in descriptive geometry, and "rzutowa" is not a noun at all; both are malformed variants of "rzut", which the file uses correctly elsewhere ("ma określony rzut wzdłuż osi z").

examples.source: the product of uncertainties ΔXΔZ … the uncertainty product dips … yields zero uncertainty in the physical observable
examples.suggested: pick one rendering for the quantity ΔS (e.g. "nieoznaczoność" throughout, keeping "zasada/relacja nieoznaczoności" for the principle)
examples.translation: iloczynu niepewności $\Delta X \Delta Z$ … iloczyn nieoznaczoności spada … daje zerową nieoznaczoność obserwowalnej fizycznej
examples.why: The same quantity ΔS is called "niepewność" in one half of the file and "nieoznaczoność" in the other; both are defensible Polish words, but a learner tracking ΔX across sections sees two apparently different concepts.

examples.source: Explain how you would push this to the absolute limit … a and b are tied … Suppose you orient a measurement device
examples.suggested: Wyjaśnij, jak doprowadzić to do absolutnej granicy, maksymalizując ⟨Y⟩. … a i b są równorzędne … Załóżmy, że ustawiasz urządzenie pomiarowe
examples.translation: Wyjaśnij, jak wypchnąć to do absolutnej granicy, czyniąc $\langle Y \rangle$ jak największym? … a i b są remisem … Przypuść, że orientujesz urządzenie pomiarowe
examples.why: "wypchnąć do granicy" is a literal calque of "push to the limit" and the imperative ends with a stray question mark; "są remisem" and the bare imperative "Przypuść" are phrasings a Polish technical writer would not use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the informal "ty" register holds ("Sampler daje ci możliwość...", "czy użyłbyś prymitywu"), but the file is split on its single most important term: "circuit" is "obwód kwantowy" in the first half (§Programming model for QPUs, §Why both?) and then an inflected English noun "Circuit" from §Task workflows onward — "Circuit kwantowy", "optymalizacji Circuitów", "budowania Circuitu `PauliTwoDesign`", "prostym Circuitem kwantowym" — even swapping mid-paragraph at line 162 ("postaci wykonywalnej kwantowo (Circuit kwantowy)... ten obwód kwantowy jest optymalizowany"). Separately, "pipeline" and "workflow" both collapse into "potok", which destroys the contrast the lesson is making: "wszystkie zadania są wykonywane jedno po drugim w potoku. Jednak w przypadku potoków zadań nie jesteśmy ograniczeni do liniowej kolejności" reads self-contradictory where the English opposes a linear pipeline to a non-linear task workflow (and §Classical programming models had already used "przepływach zadań" for the same term). Smaller items: "scheduler" → "Harmonogram" (a schedule, not the component that schedules), the typo "obserwowalana", the calque "linii (zwanych drutami)" for wires, "zbiegła się do naszych celów" for "converged sufficiently for our purposes", and two image alt texts (workflow.svg, sqd-workflow.svg) left in English while all others are translated.

examples.source: The optimized quantum circuit is then executed on the actual quantum hardware. / build a `PauliTwoDesign` circuit / the transpiled quantum circuit
examples.suggested: Zoptymalizowany obwód kwantowy ... / budowania obwodu `PauliTwoDesign` / transpilowany obwód kwantowy
examples.translation: Zoptymalizowany Circuit kwantowy jest następnie wykonywany na rzeczywistym sprzęcie kwantowym. / budowania Circuitu `PauliTwoDesign` / transpilowany Circuit kwantowy
examples.why: The file establishes the correct Polish term "obwód kwantowy" in the QPU section and then abandons it for the English noun "Circuit" declined with Polish endings (Circuitu, Circuitów, Circuitem) for the whole second half — roughly a dozen occurrences, including one paragraph that uses both renderings for the same object. Recognizable, so not misleading, but no Polish technical writer would leave it this way.

examples.source: The four steps of a Qiskit pattern are mapping, optimization, execution, and post-processing, where all tasks are executed one after another in a pipeline. But with task workflows we are not bound to a linear execution order
examples.suggested: ...wszystkie zadania są wykonywane jedno po drugim w potoku (pipeline). Jednak w przypadku przepływów zadań nie jesteśmy ograniczeni do liniowej kolejności wykonywania
examples.translation: ...wszystkie zadania są wykonywane jedno po drugim w potoku. Jednak w przypadku potoków zadań nie jesteśmy ograniczeni do liniowej kolejności wykonywania
examples.why: "pipeline" and "workflow" are both rendered "potok", so the sentence that teaches the distinction (linear pipeline vs. non-linear workflow) reads as contradicting itself. The section heading term also changed from "przepływach zadań" (used earlier at §Classical programming models) to "potok zadań" here.

examples.source: A scheduler is the component that maps tasks to resources and orchestrates execution.
examples.suggested: Program szeregujący (scheduler) to komponent, który przypisuje zadania do zasobów i organizuje ich wykonanie.
examples.translation: Harmonogram to komponent, który przypisuje zadania do zasobów i organizuje ich wykonanie.
examples.why: "Harmonogram" is the schedule (the timetable), not the scheduling component; the sentence defines it in place so the learner still gets the concept, but the noun is the wrong half of the pair and recurs at line 162 ("zarządzana i wykonywana przez harmonogram", "harmonogram współpracuje z jedną fioletową jednostką").

examples.source: a set of lines (called wires) that represent qubits / whether the ground state energy has converged sufficiently for our purposes
examples.suggested: zestawu linii (zwanych przewodami) reprezentujących kubity / czy energia stanu podstawowego zbiegła się wystarczająco dla naszych celów
examples.translation: zestawu linii (zwanych drutami) reprezentujących qubity / czy energia stanu podstawowego dostatecznie zbiegła się do naszych celów
examples.why: "drut" is a physical metal wire and reads oddly for circuit wires ("przewód" is the usual rendering); "zbiegła się do naszych celów" is a calque that literally says the energy converged *to* our purposes rather than converged sufficiently *for* them.

examples.source: (the quantum circuit converted into a qasm file, the observable, and the parameters)
examples.suggested: (obwód kwantowy przekonwertowany do pliku qasm, obserwabla i parametry)
examples.translation: (Circuit kwantowy przekonwertowany do pliku qasm, obserwowalana i parametry)
examples.why: Typo "obserwowalana" for the observable; elsewhere the file consistently uses "obserwowalna/obserwowalnej", so this is a stray misspelling in the noun the whole Estimator discussion hangs on.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — all nine notes and the two column definitions carry the English claims correctly (support levels, the "as of July 2025 / qiskit-qasm3-import v0.6.0" caveats, the "not eligible for execution on hardware" restrictions), so nothing here misleads a learner. But four things a native technical editor would fix: (1) in "Próximos passos" the English bullet "- Review the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic." was left in *and* its Portuguese rendering added on the next line, so the reader sees the same item twice, once in English; (2) "circuit" is rendered inconsistently — natural lowercase "circuito/circuitos" in most places ("criar o circuito", "circuitos dinâmicos", "Os circuitos devem ser transpilados") but left as capitalized English "Circuits" five times ("enviar Circuits ao IBM Qiskit Runtime", "apenas Circuits definidos em termos de qubits de hardware", "em Circuits ISA válidos", "execução de tais Circuits"); (3) "backend" is likewise capitalized as if a proper noun ("execução no Backend", "ISA do Backend", "alguns Backends") where Portuguese would use lowercase "backend"; (4) the sentence "O significado da marca \"suportado\" completa depende da coluna" strands the adjective and reads as calqued word order. Also, in the `qubit` table row the Qiskit class name `Qubit` was lowercased to `qubit`, collapsing the class into the OpenQASM keyword already in column 1.

examples.source: - Review the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic.
examples.suggested: Keep only the Portuguese bullet: "- Revise o tópico [Verifique seu programa](/guides/debugging-tools)."
examples.translation:
- Review the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic.
    - Revise o tópico [Verifique seu programa](./debugging-tools).
examples.why: The untranslated English source line was left in place and the Portuguese version appended below it, so the recommendations list shows the same item twice, one of them in English.

examples.source: The most common method of submitting circuits to IBM Qiskit Runtime … Circuits constructed and submitted in this manner …
examples.suggested: O método mais comum de enviar circuitos ao IBM Qiskit Runtime … Circuitos construídos e enviados dessa forma …
examples.translation: O método mais comum de enviar Circuits ao IBM Qiskit Runtime … Circuits construídos e enviados dessa forma …
examples.why: "circuit" is translated as "circuito(s)" everywhere else in the same file ("criar o circuito", "Os circuitos devem ser transpilados", "circuitos dinâmicos") but left as capitalized English "Circuits" in five places — an inconsistent glossary leak, not a deliberate keep-English convention.

examples.source: backend execution always requires circuits to have been compiled to the backend Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)
examples.suggested: a execução no backend sempre exige que os circuitos tenham sido compilados para a Arquitetura de Conjunto de Instruções (ISA) do backend
examples.translation: a execução no Backend sempre exige que os circuitos tenham sido compilados para a Arquitetura de Conjunto de Instruções (ISA) do Backend
examples.why: "backend" is a common noun kept in English in Portuguese Qiskit docs; capitalizing it mid-sentence ("no Backend", "do Backend", "alguns Backends") reads as a German-style artifact, not Portuguese usage.

examples.source: The meaning of the complete "supported" mark depends on the column:
examples.suggested: O significado da marca "suportado" (suporte completo) depende da coluna:
examples.translation: O significado da marca "suportado" completa depende da coluna:
examples.why: The adjective "completa" is stranded after the quoted term, producing word order no Portuguese technical writer would use; the reader has to reparse to see that "completa" modifies "marca".

examples.source: | `qubit` | `Qubit` and `QuantumRegister` |
examples.suggested: | `qubit` | `Qubit` e `QuantumRegister` |
examples.translation: | `qubit` | `qubit` and `QuantumRegister` |
examples.why: The Qiskit class name `Qubit` was lowercased to `qubit`, so the "Qiskit SDK feature" cell now repeats the OpenQASM keyword from column 1 instead of naming the Python class it maps to (the row for `bit` correctly keeps `Clbit`).

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the informal "você" register holds ("mas você pode usar as primitivas base em vez disso"); core terms are right and consistent (valor esperado, primitivas, observável, lote, transpilar, job/backend/shots kept in English as the field does). The one real defect is that "circuit" is rendered two ways inside the same file: it is left as untranslated, capitalized English in "um par Circuit-observável único" (line 43), "múltiplos pares Circuit-observável" (line 87) and the heading "Executar Circuits parametrizados" (line 141) — the last even carrying the English plural -s — while the very next sentence and later prose correctly say "circuito" ("aumentar a reutilização do circuito", "otimizar o desempenho do circuito nas QPUs"). This looks like a glossary keep-English rule over-firing on a common noun; it is recognizable, not misleading, but a native editor would normalize all of them to "circuito(s)". Minor secondary stiffness: "Explore o [modo de execução](/guides/execution-modes) em lote" splits the noun phrase awkwardly around the link, where "Explore o [modo de execução](/guides/execution-modes) em lote" reads better as "Explore o modo de execução em lote".
