examples.why: The English noun is inserted uninflected, so Czech case marking is lost after prepositions/numerals, and the same word appears as both 'qubit' and capitalized 'Qubit' within one sentence. Recognizable, but no Czech technical writer would leave it undeclined.

examples.source: stored the backend information … user access for most backend properties … the backend's attributes … the version of the backend itself
examples.suggested: ukládala informace o backendu … přístup k většině vlastností backendu … atributy backendu … o verzi samotného backendu
examples.translation: ukládala informace o Backend … uživatelský přístup k většině vlastností Backend … atributy Backend … o verzi samotného Backend
examples.why: 'Backend' is kept capitalized and uninflected in four different case contexts. Czech has a fully naturalized 'backend/backendu'; the frozen capitalized form reads as machine output, not prose.

examples.source: It is expected that existing providers will deprecate the old access where possible to provide a graceful migration
examples.suggested: Očekává se, že stávající poskytovatelé tam, kde to půjde, označí starý přístup jako zastaralý, aby umožnili plynulou migraci
examples.translation: Očekává se, že stávající poskytovatelé postupně označí starý přístup jako zastaralý, aby umožnili plynulou migraci
examples.why: The hedge 'where possible' is dropped and replaced by 'postupně' (gradually), which the English does not say. It slightly overstates that deprecation will happen everywhere, and swaps a scope qualifier for a timing one.

examples.source: the backend's attributes often query its BackendV2.target attribute to return information / Scroll to the right to see important notes.
examples.suggested: atributy backendu se často dotazují jeho atributu BackendV2.target, aby vrátily informace / Důležité poznámky zobrazíš posunutím doprava.
examples.translation: atributy Backend často dotazují jeho atribut BackendV2.target pro vrácení informací / Posuň se doprava pro zobrazení důležitých poznámek.
examples.why: Both render an English purpose infinitive as a bare 'pro + verbal noun' calque, and 'dotazují' is missing the reflexive 'se' that Czech requires here. Grammatically parseable but distinctly translationese.

editor_note: The prose is otherwise genuinely native and pedagogically faithful (e.g. "spolčení podezřelí v oddělených místnostech, kteří se snaží udržet svou verzi příběhu", "Cirelsonova nerovnost" correctly Czech-transliterated with the English gloss), but three things need fixing. (1) The final sentence of the EN "Remarks" section is missing entirely — the Czech file ends at "...jak provázání *pozorovat*." and drops "The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics acknowledges the importance of this line of work: the prize was awarded to Alain Aspect, John Clauser (the C in CHSH) and Anton Zeilinger for observing entanglement through Bell tests on entangled photons." (grep for "Nobel" returns nothing). (2) An untranslated-glossary leak leaves bare English "Circuit"/"Gate" embedded in Czech grammar in lines ~285-291: "diagram kvantového Circuit" (should be "diagram kvantového obvodu"), "dvě obyčejné podmíněné Gate", "jiný typ podmíněné Gate" — Czech uses "hradlo"/"řízené hradlo"; the words are also left uninflected, which is ungrammatical. (3) "qubit" is capitalized inconsistently within the file — lowercase "qubit $\mathsf{A}$" in the Set-up bullet but capitalized "dva Qubity", "na svém Qubitu", "stav dvou Qubitů" throughout the case analysis; also "stavový vektor qubit" (line 141) is missing the genitive "qubitu".

examples.source: The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics acknowledges the importance of this line of work: the prize was awarded to Alain Aspect, John Clauser (the C in CHSH) and Anton Zeilinger for observing entanglement through Bell tests on entangled photons.
examples.suggested: Nobelova cena za fyziku za rok 2022 potvrzuje důležitost této linie výzkumu: byla udělena Alainu Aspectovi, Johnu Clauserovi (písmeno C v CHSH) a Antonu Zeilingerovi za pozorování provázání pomocí Bellových testů na provázaných fotonech.
examples.translation: (missing — the Czech file ends at "...hra CHSH nám dává konkrétní a testovatelný způsob, jak provázání *pozorovat*.")
examples.why: A whole closing sentence of source content is dropped. It is the empirical payoff of the paragraph that just claimed "To nám poskytuje vysokou míru jistoty, že provázání je skutečné" — the Czech reader loses the concrete evidence (and the CHSH/Clauser tie-back) that grounds that claim.

examples.source: Here is a quantum circuit diagram that describes this strategy:
examples.suggested: Zde je diagram kvantového obvodu, který popisuje tuto strategii:
examples.translation: Zde je diagram kvantového Circuit, který popisuje tuto strategii:
examples.why: Untranslated English "Circuit" left inside a Czech noun phrase and uninflected — "kvantového Circuit" is ungrammatical. The standard Czech term is "kvantový obvod" (gen. "kvantového obvodu"), and the rest of the file otherwise translates domain vocabulary.

examples.source: In this diagram we see two ordinary controlled gates ... We also have two gates that look like controlled gates ... This denotes a different type of controlled gate where the gate is performed if the control is set to 0 (rather than 1 like an ordinary controlled gate).
examples.suggested: V tomto diagramu vidíme dvě obyčejná řízená hradla ... Máme také dvě hradla, která vypadají jako řízená hradla ... To označuje jiný typ řízeného hradla, kde se hradlo provede, pokud je řídicí qubit nastaven na $0$ (na rozdíl od $1$ u obyčejného řízeného hradla).
examples.translation: V tomto diagramu vidíme dvě obyčejné podmíněné Gate ... Máme také dvě Gate, které vypadají jako podmíněné Gate ... To označuje jiný typ podmíněné Gate, kde se operace provede, pokud je řídící qubit nastaven na $0$ (na rozdíl od $1$ u obyčejné podmíněné Gate).
examples.why: "Gate" is left in English five times in three sentences and cannot take Czech case/gender endings, so agreement collapses. Also "podmíněné" (conditional) is not the conventional Czech rendering of *controlled* — the field uses "řízené hradlo", and the same paragraph already says "řídící qubit", so the file contradicts itself on the same root.

examples.source: together the two qubits (A,B) are in the |phi+> state / Bob performs U on his qubit / the state of the two qubits (A,B)
examples.suggested: tyto dva qubity ... na svém qubitu ... stav dvou qubitů
examples.translation: tyto dva Qubity $(\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B})$ ... na svém Qubitu ... stav dvou Qubitů $(\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B})$
examples.why: Mid-sentence capitalization of "Qubit" is not Czech orthography and clashes with the correctly lowercase "qubit $\mathsf{A}$" / "qubit $\mathsf{B}$" a few lines earlier in the same bullet — a within-file inconsistency that reads as a leftover from an automated term substitution.

examples.source: The first thing we need to do is to define a qubit state vector |psi_theta>, for each real number theta
examples.suggested: Prvním krokem je definovat stavový vektor qubitu $\vert \psi_{\theta}\rangle$ pro každé reálné číslo $\theta$
examples.translation: Prvním krokem je definovat stavový vektor qubit $\vert \psi_{\theta}\rangle$ pro každé reálné číslo $\theta$
examples.why: "vektor qubit" is an English noun-noun compound copied straight through; Czech needs the genitive "stavový vektor qubitu". Grammatically wrong rather than merely stiff.

examples.source: let us briefly acknowledge that ... / there are no complex conjugates to worry about ... / This happens to be the optimal winning probability
examples.suggested: ...si krátce poznamenejme / uveďme, že ... / nemusíme se starat o komplexně sdružené hodnoty ... / Shodou okolností jde o *optimální* pravděpodobnost výhry
examples.translation: si krátce připusťme, že je zajímavé uvažovat i o jiných nelokálních hrách ... nemusíme se starat o komplexní sdružení ... Náhodou se jedná o *optimální* pravděpodobnost výhry
examples.why: Three calques of English idiom: "připusťme" reads as *concede* rather than the neutral *acknowledge/note*; "komplexní sdružení" names the operation, not the conjugate values the sentence is about; and "Náhodou" sounds like *by accident* where the English "happens to be" is a neutral discourse marker. None mislead, but a native technical editor would reword all three.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads a learner: meaning is faithful throughout (the verifiability caveat, the "nicht tiefeneffizient" scaling trade-off and the "auf Kosten erhöhten klassischen Rechenaufwands" caveat all survive intact), the du-register holds everywhere, and the domain terms are correct and consistently split — Fehlerminderung / Fehlerunterdrückung / Fehlererkennung, Observablen, Erwartungswerte, Verschränkung, Sampler-/Estimator-Primitive, Transpilation, Shot-für-Shot. What a native editor would still fix is small and stylistic: "Benchmark dynamic circuits with cut Bell pairs" was parsed as a noun ("Benchmark für dynamische Schaltungen …") rather than the English imperative, so the title reads as a benchmark *for* circuits instead of an instruction to benchmark them; "die effiziente Orchestrierung klassischer und Quantenressourcen" coordinates an adjective with a compound noun, which no German technical writer would leave standing; the Application-functions bullet stacks three "mit" in one sentence and line 18 says "den gesamten Ablauf eines bestimmten Workflows" (Ablauf and Workflow are the same word twice); and "Trotterisierte Schaltungsansätze" capitalizes a mid-sentence adjective that should be lowercase "trotterisierte". Separately, and outside the prose remit: the DE file imports TutorialFeedback but never renders <TutorialFeedback />, which EN has at its final line — the import is left dangling.

examples.source: Benchmark dynamic circuits with cut Bell pairs
examples.suggested: Dynamische Schaltungen mit geschnittenen Bell-Paaren benchmarken
examples.translation: Benchmark für dynamische Schaltungen mit geschnittenen Bell-Paaren
examples.why: The English is an imperative verb ('benchmark these circuits'); the German re-reads 'Benchmark' as a noun, turning an instruction into a label. Not misleading about the physics, but it breaks the parallel imperative style of the surrounding tutorial titles.

examples.source: efficient orchestration of classical and quantum resources
examples.suggested: die effiziente Orchestrierung klassischer und quantenbasierter Ressourcen
examples.translation: die effiziente Orchestrierung klassischer und Quantenressourcen
examples.why: Coordinating the inflected adjective 'klassischer' with the compound noun 'Quantenressourcen' leaves 'klassischer' syntactically stranded — a calque of the English 'classical and quantum resources' that a German technical writer would resolve by adjectivizing both halves.

examples.source: to improve part or the whole of a particular workflow
examples.suggested: um einen Teil oder den gesamten Workflow zu verbessern
examples.translation: um einen Teil oder den gesamten Ablauf eines bestimmten Workflows zu verbessern
examples.why: 'Ablauf eines … Workflows' says the same word twice; the English has no second noun. Harmless but visibly translated rather than written.

examples.source: Techniques include both variational and Trotterized circuit approaches
examples.suggested: … sowohl variationelle als auch trotterisierte Schaltungsansätze
examples.translation: Zu den Techniken gehören sowohl variationelle als auch Trotterisierte Schaltungsansätze
examples.why: 'Trotterisierte' is an attributive adjective and must be lowercase in German; the capital is carried over from English title-style capitalization. Purely orthographic, but it sits next to correctly lowercased 'variationelle' in the same phrase, so the inconsistency is conspicuous.

editor_note: Mathematically faithful throughout — Spektralsatz/Spektralzerlegung, normale/hermitesche Matrizen, Eigenwert/Eigenvektor, Einheitskreis and the "du"-register (Beachte, Betrachte, Sei) are all correct and consistent, and no claim, condition or quantity is altered. What a native editor would still change: remark 3 contains the ungrammatical MT artifact "beginnend bei ... und bewegend uns gegen den Uhrzeigersinn" (a calqued English present participle; German needs "und bewegen uns" or "wobei wir uns ... bewegen"). "We'll discuss shortly" (= soon) becomes "Wir werden kurz darauf eingehen", which a German reader parses as "we'll touch on it briefly" — the temporal cue is lost and replaced by a brevity claim the English does not make. Smaller calques: the standalone heading-like "Expliziter:" for "More explicitly", "ist nicht spezifisch darüber, was ... ausmacht" for "isn't specific about", "einen Nicht-Null-Vektor" where German mathematics writes "einen von null verschiedenen Vektor", and the dropped discourse marker "More precisely" (Genauer gesagt) before "Da $\lambda$ auf dem komplexen Einheitskreis liegt". None of these would mislead a learner about the phase-estimation problem itself.

examples.source: starting from $e^{2\pi i \cdot 0} = 1$ and moving counter-clockwise toward $e^{2\pi i \cdot 1} = 1.$
examples.suggested: beginnend bei $e^{2\pi i \cdot 0} = 1$, und bewegen uns gegen den Uhrzeigersinn in Richtung $e^{2\pi i \cdot 1} = 1$.
examples.translation: beginnend bei $e^{2\pi i \cdot 0} = 1$ und bewegend uns gegen den Uhrzeigersinn in Richtung $e^{2\pi i \cdot 1} = 1$.
examples.why: "bewegend uns" is not grammatical German — it is a word-for-word calque of the English present participle "moving us". A native technical writer would use a finite verb or "wobei wir uns ... bewegen".

examples.source: We'll discuss shortly how the precision we require affects the computational cost of a solution.
examples.suggested: Wir werden in Kürze besprechen, wie die geforderte Genauigkeit die Berechnungskosten einer Lösung beeinflusst.
examples.translation: Wir werden kurz darauf eingehen, wie die geforderte Genauigkeit die Berechnungskosten einer Lösung beeinflusst.
examples.why: English "shortly" is temporal (soon, later in the lesson); "kurz darauf eingehen" reads as "treat it briefly", i.e. a promise about depth rather than timing — a small unintended claim about how much the topic will be covered.

examples.source: More explicitly,
examples.suggested: Ausgeschrieben lautet das:
examples.translation: Expliziter:
examples.why: A bare comparative adverb used as a standalone connector is un-German and reads as MT; German prose would use "Ausgeschrieben:", "Konkret:" or "Genauer gesagt:".

examples.source: The statement of the phase estimation problem above isn't specific about what constitutes an approximation of $\theta$
examples.suggested: Die obige Formulierung des Phasenschätzungsproblems legt nicht genau fest, was als Approximation von $\theta$ gilt
examples.translation: Die obige Formulierung des Phasenschätzungsproblems ist nicht spezifisch darüber, was eine Approximation von $\theta$ ausmacht
examples.why: "ist nicht spezifisch darüber" is a direct calque of "isn't specific about"; the German idiom is "legt nicht fest" / "präzisiert nicht".

examples.source: a non-zero vector $\vert\psi\rangle$
examples.suggested: einen von null verschiedenen Vektor $\vert\psi\rangle$
examples.translation: einen Nicht-Null-Vektor $\vert\psi\rangle$
examples.why: Recognizable but not the conventional German mathematical phrasing; "Nicht-Null-Vektor" is a hyphenated calque where textbooks write "von null verschieden" or "vom Nullvektor verschieden".

examples.source: More precisely, because $\lambda$ lies on the complex unit circle, we can write
examples.suggested: Genauer gesagt: Da $\lambda$ auf dem komplexen Einheitskreis liegt, können wir
examples.translation: Da $\lambda$ auf dem komplexen Einheitskreis liegt, können wir
examples.why: The dropped "More precisely" is the signal that the following equation sharpens the goal just stated (compute/approximate $\lambda$ → compute $\theta$); without it the sentence reads as a new fact rather than a refinement of the preceding one.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift found: the TTL logic ("Los trabajos que estén en ejecución terminarán, pero los trabajos aún en cola fallarán"), the close-vs-cancel bullet list, and the four session states (with helpful added Spanish glosses "(En progreso, no acepta nuevos trabajos)") all match the English exactly, and the tú register is consistent (Usa, Puedes, debes, Prueba, Consulta, Revisa). What a native editor would change is the untranslated anglicism "workload": it appears ~11 times in prose with Spanish articles ("Los workloads deben ejecutarse…", "un workload iterativo", "cada workload") where Spanish IBM/cloud docs say "cargas de trabajo" — note the file already translates the neighbouring concept as "trabajos", so "workload" sits oddly next to it. Secondary nits: the QAOA link title "Algoritmo de optimización aproximada cuántica" is an English-word-order calque (standard is "Algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada"), and line 241 repeats "estado…estado" ("consultar el estado de una sesión para entender su estado actual") where English varies status/state. None of these mislead a learner.

examples.source: Workloads must be run in job mode or batch mode. / Run an iterative workload… / running multiple workloads simultaneously
examples.suggested: Las cargas de trabajo deben ejecutarse… / ejecuta una carga de trabajo iterativa… / ejecutando varias cargas de trabajo simultáneamente
examples.translation: Los workloads deben ejecutarse en modo de trabajo o modo por lotes. / ejecuta un workload iterativo… / ejecutando múltiples workloads simultáneamente
examples.why: "Workload" is not a term the quantum field keeps in English in Spanish; IBM Spanish documentation renders it "cargas de trabajo". Left untranslated ~11 times in prose it reads as an anglicism, and it sits awkwardly beside the correctly translated "trabajos" (jobs) in the same sentence. (The console page name "Workloads" on line 241 is correctly left as-is — that is a UI label.)

examples.source: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA)
examples.suggested: Algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada (QAOA)
examples.translation: Algoritmo de optimización aproximada cuántica (QAOA)
examples.why: English word order is calqued, so "cuántica" ends up modifying "optimización aproximada" rather than "algoritmo". The established Spanish rendering puts "cuántico" on the algorithm. Not misleading (the QAOA acronym disambiguates) but a native editor would reorder it.

examples.source: You can query a session's status to understand its current state by using session.status()…
examples.suggested: Puedes consultar el estado de una sesión para conocer su situación actual con `session.status()`…
examples.translation: Puedes consultar el estado de una sesión para entender su estado actual usando `session.status()`…
examples.why: English distinguishes status/state; Spanish collapses both to "estado", producing a clumsy "el estado … su estado actual" repetition in one clause. A native technical writer would vary the second noun or drop it.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: meaning is faithful throughout and the core terminology is correct and consistent (transpile→transpilar/transpilación, pass manager→gestor de pases, staged→por etapas, preset→preconfigurado, transpiler pass→pase de transpilador, qubit and backend kept in English, "no hay límite en el número de etapas" matches the English claim, and the `generate_embed_passmanager` sentence keeps the "a partir de un pase de layout hacia el dispositivo objetivo especificado" direction intact). Two things a native technical editor would still change. First, one English-passive calque in the opening explanation: "El circuito es procesado por cada pase del transpilador en secuencia" — Spanish technical prose would use an active or reflexive construction ("Cada pase del transpilador procesa el circuito en secuencia" / "El circuito se procesa..."). Second, the instructional voice in the section headings is inconsistent: "## Generar un gestor de pases por etapas preconfigurado" uses the infinitive while the two parallel headings use the tú imperative ("## Crea tu propio gestor de pases", "## Crea un gestor de pases por etapas"), so the English's uniform imperative parallelism is broken. Body register is otherwise solidly informal tú throughout (consulta, utiliza, pasa, llama, inicializa, pruébalo, Revisa) with no usted slips.

examples.source: The circuit is processed by each transpiler pass in sequence, with the output of one pass becoming the input to the next.
examples.suggested: Cada pase del transpilador procesa el circuito en secuencia: la salida de un pase se convierte en la entrada del siguiente.
examples.translation: El circuito es procesado por cada pase del transpilador en secuencia, donde la salida de un pase se convierte en la entrada del siguiente.
examples.why: "es procesado por" is a direct calque of the English agentive passive; Spanish technical writing strongly prefers the active or reflexive form here. Grammatical but reads as machine output rather than something a Spanish-speaking engineer would write. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: ## Generate a preset staged pass manager
examples.suggested: ## Genera un gestor de pases por etapas preconfigurado
examples.translation: ## Generar un gestor de pases por etapas preconfigurado
examples.why: The other two task headings in the same file use the tú imperative ("## Crea tu propio gestor de pases", "## Crea un gestor de pases por etapas"), so this infinitive breaks the parallel instructional voice the English maintains across all three headings.

editor_note: No semantic drift anywhere: every claim matches the English, including the counter-intuitive pair "toutes les données client sont transmises sur le réseau privé, que ce soit via un point de terminaison public ou via VPE" / "IBM Quantum Platform n'est accessible que via le réseau public", and the informal "tu" register holds throughout with no vous/votre/veuillez slip. What a native technical editor would change are three infrastructure-terminology calques in the second paragraph: "créée sur une base par service" is a word-for-word tracing of "on a per-service basis" (French says "créée pour chaque service" or simply "par service"); "est redondante et très disponible" renders the fixed industry term "highly available" literally instead of "à haute disponibilité"; and "s'adapte horizontalement" is weaker than the standard "évolue horizontalement" / "à mise à l'échelle horizontale". Also cosmetic: "les Points de Terminaison Privés Virtuels" carries English title-case capitalization that French does not use. None of these would mislead a learner — the concepts stay identifiable — but the paragraph reads as translated rather than written.

examples.source: VPEs are virtual IP interfaces that are bound to an endpoint gateway created on a per-service basis.
examples.suggested: Les VPE sont des interfaces IP virtuelles liées à une passerelle de point de terminaison créée pour chaque service.
examples.translation: Les VPE sont des interfaces IP virtuelles liées à une passerelle de point de terminaison créée sur une base par service.
examples.why: "sur une base par service" is a literal tracing of "on a per-service basis"; the construction does not exist in French technical prose, which uses "pour chaque service" or simply "par service".

examples.source: a virtualized function that scales horizontally, is redundant and highly available
examples.suggested: une fonction virtualisée à mise à l'échelle horizontale, redondante et à haute disponibilité
examples.translation: une fonction virtualisée qui s'adapte horizontalement, est redondante et très disponible
examples.why: "highly available" is a fixed cloud-infrastructure term rendered in French as "à haute disponibilité"; "très disponible" reads as an everyday adjective and loses the technical sense. "s'adapte horizontalement" likewise understates "scales horizontally" (évolue horizontalement / mise à l'échelle horizontale).

examples.source: Use Virtual Private Endpoints (VPE) for VPC to connect to IBM Quantum...
examples.suggested: Utilise les points de terminaison privés virtuels (VPE) pour VPC afin de te connecter à IBM Quantum...
examples.translation: Utilise les Points de Terminaison Privés Virtuels (VPE) pour VPC afin de te connecter à IBM Quantum...
examples.why: English title-case capitalization carried over onto a common noun phrase; French capitalizes only the first word (the rest of the file already writes "passerelle de point de terminaison" in lower case, so it is also internally inconsistent).

editor_note: The prose is idiomatic, faithful and reads as natively written French IAM documentation — the tricky negated caveat in step 11 is preserved exactly ("si tu ne définis pas la portée de l'accès sur Toutes les ressources, le rôle Analytics Viewer ne pourra pas voir les analyses de toutes les instances"), the "tu" register holds throughout with no vous/votre/veuillez slips, and IBM Cloud UI labels are handled coherently (Gérer → IAM → Groupes d'accès, Attribuer un accès +, Accès personnalisé). The one thing a native technical editor would change: the IBM Cloud role name "Viewer" is rendered two different ways inside the same file — translated as "Observateur" in the intro list of pre-configured roles (line 11, "exemples : Éditeur, Observateur, Opérateur"), then left in English at the point where the reader actually has to find it in the UI ("coche la case Viewer (sous Plateforme)", line 57, and "ainsi que le rôle Viewer", line 59). Nothing here misleads — the steps still teach the same procedure as the English — but the split means a reader who learned "Observateur" in the intro has to re-identify it as "Viewer" three sections later; harmonizing on the English UI label in both places (or glossing it once) would fix it.

examples.source: they assign roles (example: Editor, Viewer, Operator, and so on) … check the Viewer box (under Platform) … your custom role as well as the Viewer role
examples.suggested: ils attribuent des rôles (exemples : Editor, Viewer, Operator, etc.)
examples.translation: ils attribuent des rôles (exemples : Éditeur, Observateur, Opérateur, etc.) … coche la case Viewer (sous Plateforme) … ton rôle personnalisé ainsi que le rôle Viewer
examples.why: The same IBM Cloud role name is rendered "Observateur" in the introduction and left as "Viewer" in the click-path steps, so the reader cannot tell they are the same role. Since steps 12–13 require finding the literal checkbox in the console, the English label should be used in both places (Editor/Operator likewise).

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the option list, the min_qpy_version security caveat ("מטענים עוינים אפשריים"), the QISKIT_FORCE_THREADS serial-execution explanation and the SABRE ">20 CPUs/cores, results not reproducible on different local hardware" tradeoff all land correctly, and the informal imperative register (הגדר / נסה / הרץ / קרא) is consistent. Four things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "circuit drawer" is rendered three ways in the same file — "לצייר Circuit" (line 33, which parses as the verb "to draw a circuit" rather than the noun "the drawer"), "מערכת ציור" (line 33) and "צייר ה-Circuit" (lines 34, 35, 43); pick "צייר ה-Circuit" everywhere. (2) "state visualization" → "הדמיית מצב" (lines 36, 44): in Hebrew CS usage הדמיה is normally *simulation*, which in a quantum context collides with statevector simulation; "המחשה חזותית של המצב" is the safer reading. (3) line 54 drops the English hedge "potentially" and hardens it into a definite claim ("משאבי ה-CPU המוגבלים"). (4) line 62 "לתרום ל-Qiskit SDK בקוד פתוח" is a calqued word order for "the open-source Qiskit SDK". None of these would mislead a learner about how Qiskit behaves.

examples.source: Changes the default system for the circuit drawer. ... When the output kwarg is not explicitly set, this drawer system is used.
examples.suggested: משנה את מערכת ברירת המחדל של צייר ה-Circuit. ... נעשה שימוש במערכת ציור זו של צייר ה-Circuit.
examples.translation: משנה את מערכת ברירת המחדל לצייר Circuit. ... נעשה שימוש במערכת ציור זו.
examples.why: The same noun "circuit drawer" appears as "לצייר Circuit" (reads as the infinitive "to draw a circuit", not as the tool), "מערכת ציור", and "צייר ה-Circuit" within a few lines. The concept stays identifiable, so this is within-file inconsistency, not a false concept — but a native editor would unify on "צייר ה-Circuit", which the file already uses in lines 34/35/43.

examples.source: This is used to change the default system for the state visualization draw methods. ... State visualization draw methods are ...
examples.suggested: משמש לשינוי מערכת ברירת המחדל של שיטות הציור להמחשה חזותית של המצב. ... שיטות הציור להמחשה חזותית של המצב הן ...
examples.translation: משמש לשינוי מערכת ברירת המחדל לשיטות ציור הדמיית מצב. ... שיטות ציור הדמיית מצב הן ...
examples.why: In Hebrew technical writing הדמיה is the standard word for *simulation*; in a quantum-computing page that word collides with state/statevector simulation, a different operation entirely. The adjacent "שיטות ציור" keeps the reader on track, so it is imperfect-but-recognizable rather than misleading, but המחשה חזותית / הצגה חזותית is the right register here.

examples.source: This is done to avoid potentially overloading limited CPU resources.
examples.suggested: זה נעשה כדי להימנע מעומס יתר אפשרי על משאבי CPU מוגבלים.
examples.translation: זה נעשה כדי להימנע מעומס יתר על משאבי ה-CPU המוגבלים.
examples.why: The English hedges twice — "potentially" and indefinite "limited CPU resources". The Hebrew drops the hedge and adds the definite article ("משאבי ה-CPU המוגבלים"), asserting both that overload would happen and that the reader's CPU resources are limited. A dropped qualifier, but it does not change what the flag does, so MINOR rather than a misleading claim.

examples.source: Read the contributing guidelines if you want to contribute to the open-source Qiskit SDK.
examples.suggested: קרא את הנחיות התרומה אם ברצונך לתרום ל-Qiskit SDK, שהוא פרויקט קוד פתוח.
examples.translation: קרא את הנחיות התרומה אם ברצונך לתרום ל-Qiskit SDK בקוד פתוח.
examples.why: "לתרום ל-Qiskit SDK בקוד פתוח" calques the English attributive "open-source X" into a trailing adverbial, so it reads as "contribute in open source" rather than "contribute to the open-source SDK". A Hebrew technical writer would use an appositive or "לקוד הפתוח של Qiskit SDK".

editor_note: No semantic drift: the "value set after initialization wins" rule, the [1, 10800] range with its 10800 (3 שעות) default, and every incompatibility list are faithful, and the informal register holds throughout (ניתן להשתמש, השתמש במתודת). Two things a native technical editor would change. (1) Terminology: "ground state" is rendered "מצב הבסיס" (line ~151) — the conventional Hebrew physics term is "מצב היסוד"; "מצב הבסיס" reads as *basis* state and blurs the concept, though the surrounding "לאפס את ה-Qubits ... לכל shot" keeps it recoverable. Also "**Choices**" is rendered "**אפשרויות**" — the same word this whole page uses for "options" — so on a page about options the value lists read as "אפשרויות: None"; "ערכים אפשריים" would keep the two apart. (2) Fluency/agreement: "when using X" is clipped to the calque "בשימוש ב-`qiskit-ibm-runtime` v0.42.0" (lines ~202, ~216, ~226) instead of "בעת שימוש ב-", and every tab opens with masculine-singular "אינו תואם עם" even where the subject is plural ("מעגלים דינמיים" → should be "אינם תואמים"), plus "תואם עם" is itself an English-shaped collocation (Hebrew takes "תואם ל-" / "אינו תואם את"). Addressee form also flips: singular imperatives ציין / השתמש / לחץ / עיין against plural בקרו ... ובחרו in the "Available options" intro.

examples.source: Whether to reset the qubits to the ground state for each shot.
examples.suggested: האם לאפס את ה-Qubits למצב היסוד בכל shot.
examples.translation: האם לאפס את ה-Qubits למצב הבסיס לכל shot.
examples.why: "ground state" is מצב היסוד in Hebrew physics usage; מצב הבסיס reads as "basis state" (מצב בסיס), a different concept — recognizable in context, but the wrong domain term.

examples.source: **Choices**: None / DEBUG, INFO, ...
examples.suggested: **ערכים אפשריים**: ...
examples.translation: **אפשרויות**: None / DEBUG, INFO, ...
examples.why: "Choices" collapses onto the same word used for "options" everywhere else on the page (אפשרויות), so the value list and the option itself share one label.

examples.source: Compatible with fractional gates when using `qiskit-ibm-runtime` v0.42.0 or later.
examples.suggested: תואם לשערים שבריים בעת שימוש ב-`qiskit-ibm-runtime` v0.42.0 ואילך.
examples.translation: תואם עם שערים שברים בשימוש ב-`qiskit-ibm-runtime` v0.42.0 ומעלה.
examples.why: "בשימוש ב-" is a clipped calque of "when using" that no Hebrew technical writer would use bare; "תואם עם" mirrors English "compatible with" where Hebrew takes תואם ל-.

examples.source: Incompatible with: - Gate-folding ZNE ...
examples.suggested: אינם תואמים ל-: ... (in the Dynamic-circuits and fractional-gates tabs)
examples.translation: אינו תואם עם: ...
examples.why: Masculine-singular אינו is used under tabs whose subject is plural (מעגלים דינמיים, שערים שברים); a native editor would fix the agreement rather than leave a frozen impersonal formula.

examples.source: visit the [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` API reference](...) and select a previous version.
examples.suggested: היכנס ל[הפניית ה-API של `qiskit-ibm-runtime`](...) ובחר גרסה קודמת.
examples.translation: בקרו ב[הפניית API של `qiskit-ibm-runtime`](...) ובחרו גרסה קודמת.
examples.why: Plural imperatives here clash with the singular imperatives used elsewhere in the file (ציין, השתמש, לחץ, עיין); pick one addressee. "בקרו ב" is also a web-marketing calque for a docs page.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the resilience-level table, the "level 1 + turn off measurement mitigation" caveat, and the "resilience_level 0 vs zne_mitigation = True overrides" example all land correctly, and domain terms are handled sensibly (noise, twirling, ZNE/TREX, overhead, trade-off kept in English; "penekanan error" for error suppression used consistently). Two editorial defects remain. First, "circuit" is rendered inconsistently and with a capital-letter glossary artifact: "sirkuit" (lowercase) appears once, but "Circuit" capitalized mid-sentence appears three times — worst inside a single clause, "bervariasi dari satu sirkuit ke Circuit lainnya", plus "ansambel, Circuit yang saling berkaitan" and "semua jenis Circuit". Second, the informal-register convention breaks: the file uses "-mu" forms ("hasilmu", "jobmu", "primitifmu", "Kamu bisa") but switches to "Anda" four times, including within one sentence ("Kamu bisa menggunakan level resilience ... atau Anda bisa mengatur teknik kustom"). Minor stiffness also in the table cell "Pengukuran twirling [TREX]", where Indonesian head-first order wants "twirling pengukuran".

examples.source: solution quality will vary from circuit to circuit
examples.suggested: kualitas solusi akan bervariasi dari satu sirkuit ke sirkuit lainnya
examples.translation: kualitas solusi akan bervariasi dari satu sirkuit ke Circuit lainnya
examples.why: The same noun is rendered two ways inside one clause, and the capitalized "Circuit" is a glossary-substitution artifact that reads as a proper noun/class name rather than the physical circuit.

examples.source: processing the outputs from a collection, or ensemble, of related circuits
examples.suggested: memproses output dari kumpulan, atau ansambel, sirkuit yang saling berkaitan
examples.translation: memproses output dari kumpulan, atau ansambel, Circuit yang saling berkaitan
examples.why: Same capitalized-"Circuit" artifact; also breaks Indonesian sentence casing mid-clause. Same issue again at "semua jenis Circuit" in the compatibility admonition.

examples.source: You can use resilience levels to specify noise management techniques, or you can set custom techniques individually
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa menggunakan level resilience untuk menentukan teknik manajemen noise, atau kamu bisa mengatur teknik kustom secara individual
examples.translation: Kamu bisa menggunakan level resilience untuk menentukan teknik manajemen noise, atau Anda bisa mengatur teknik kustom secara individual
examples.why: The two English "you"s in one sentence become "Kamu" then "Anda". The file elsewhere commits to informal -mu forms (hasilmu, jobmu, primitifmu), so the switch is a visible register slip within a single sentence.

examples.source: Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX) measurement twirling
examples.suggested: twirling pengukuran [Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX)]
examples.translation: Pengukuran twirling [Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX)]
examples.why: English-order noun stacking calqued into Indonesian: "Pengukuran twirling" reads as "a twirling measurement", whereas the technique is measurement twirling — Indonesian puts the head noun first, "twirling pengukuran".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I verified the parity/eigenvalue mapping (even parity → +1, odd → −1), the commute→+1 / anti-commute→−1 logic, the "64 Pauli operations, exactly 16 in this category" count, the four 2-dimensional subspaces, and the X⊗X⊗X logical-X aside; nothing is inverted, softened or dropped, and core terms (generator stabilizer, sindrom, ruang kode, observable, eigenvector/eigenvalue) are correct and consistent. What a native editor would change is style: "Circuit" and "Gate" are capitalized mid-sentence (L36/37/39/41 "menggunakan Circuit yang disarankan", "Circuit pengecekan paritas"; L156 "Gate $X$") while every other retained English term — qubit, state, observable, encoding, eigenvector — is lowercase, an inconsistent glossary-injection artifact; native usage would be lowercase "sirkuit"/"gerbang". Several calques remain: L12 "melihat kedua kalinya kode repetisi 3-bit" for "take a second look", L76/L101 "beraksi trivial pada" for "acts trivially", L100 "selalu akan satu atau yang lain", L155 "pada titik ini" plus the broken italic scope in "tapi *bukan sendiri* proporsional", and L137 "sehingga mereka adalah vektor unit" using the animate pronoun "mereka" for subspaces. Informal register ("kita", "kamu"-level neutrality, no bapak/ibu) holds correctly.

examples.source: Next, we'll take a second look at the 3-bit repetition code, this time phrasing it in terms of Pauli operations.
examples.suggested: Selanjutnya, kita akan meninjau kembali kode repetisi 3-bit, kali ini merumuskannya dalam bentuk operasi Pauli.
examples.translation: Selanjutnya, kita akan melihat kedua kalinya kode repetisi 3-bit, kali ini menguraikannya dalam bentuk operasi Pauli.
examples.why: "melihat kedua kalinya" is a word-for-word rendering of "take a second look" and is not idiomatic Indonesian; the title itself already uses the correct "ditinjau ulang", so the body contradicts its own heading.

examples.source: measure both using the circuits suggested at the end of the previous section / equivalent to an X gate on the logical qubit
examples.suggested: mengukur keduanya menggunakan sirkuit yang disarankan di akhir bagian sebelumnya / setara dengan gerbang $X$ pada qubit logis
examples.translation: mengukur keduanya menggunakan Circuit yang disarankan di akhir bagian sebelumnya / setara dengan Gate $X$ pada qubit logis
examples.why: "Circuit" (4x) and "Gate" are capitalized mid-sentence like proper nouns, while all other retained English terms in the same file (qubit, state, observable, encoding, eigenvector) are lowercase — an inconsistent glossary artifact no Indonesian technical writer would produce.

examples.source: Z⊗Z⊗I acts trivially on |psi>. / the stabilizer generators act trivially on this state.
examples.suggested: $Z\otimes Z\otimes \mathbb{I}$ bekerja secara trivial pada $\vert\psi\rangle.$ / generator stabilizer bekerja secara trivial pada state ini.
examples.translation: $Z\otimes Z\otimes \mathbb{I}$ beraksi trivial pada $\vert\psi\rangle.$ / generator stabilizer beraksi trivial pada state ini.
examples.why: "beraksi trivial" is a calque of "acts trivially": Indonesian requires the adverbial "secara trivial", and "bekerja pada" is the conventional verb for an operator acting on a state.

examples.source: For errors represented by Pauli operations, it will always be one or the other, because any two Pauli operations either commute or anti-commute.
examples.suggested: Untuk kesalahan yang direpresentasikan oleh operasi Pauli, pasti salah satu dari keduanya, karena dua operasi Pauli mana pun pasti commute atau anti-commute.
examples.translation: Untuk kesalahan yang direpresentasikan oleh operasi Pauli, selalu akan satu atau yang lain, karena dua operasi Pauli mana pun selalu commute atau anti-commute.
examples.why: "selalu akan satu atau yang lain" is a literal transposition of "it will always be one or the other" with no subject; the clause reads as machine output rather than Indonesian prose.

examples.source: Although it's mainly an aside at this point, it's worth mentioning that Pauli operations that commute with both stabilizer generators ... but are not themselves proportional to elements of the stabilizer
examples.suggested: Meskipun untuk saat ini ini sekadar catatan sampingan, perlu disebutkan bahwa operasi Pauli yang commute dengan *kedua* generator stabilizer ... tetapi *sendirinya* tidak proporsional dengan elemen stabilizer
examples.translation: Meskipun ini terutama sebagai tambahan pada titik ini, perlu disebutkan bahwa operasi Pauli yang commute dengan *kedua* generator stabilizer ... tapi *bukan sendiri* proporsional dengan elemen stabilizer
examples.why: "pada titik ini" calques "at this point" (Indonesian uses "untuk saat ini"/"pada tahap ini"), and forcing the italics onto "themselves" produced the ungrammatical "bukan sendiri proporsional" — negation and reflexive are in the wrong order.

examples.source: Encodings for the 3-bit repetition code are 3-qubit states, so they're unit vectors in an 8-dimensional complex vector space.
examples.suggested: Encoding untuk kode repetisi 3-bit adalah state 3-qubit, sehingga merupakan vektor satuan dalam ruang vektor kompleks berdimensi 8.
examples.translation: Encoding untuk kode repetisi 3-bit adalah state 3-qubit, sehingga mereka adalah vektor unit dalam ruang vektor kompleks 8-dimensi.
examples.why: "mereka" is the animate/human pronoun and is a hallmark of English-to-Indonesian MT; Indonesian simply drops the pronoun here. "vektor satuan" is also the standard term for "unit vector".

editor_note: Faithful, natural HPC-Italian prose with correct English retentions (job, backend, plugin, workload manager, allocator/remote context names) and correct domain renderings ("carichi di lavoro quantistici", "primitive QRMI", "file header di Slurm", "Le risorse non documentate verranno escluse"); informal "tu" holds throughout (Puoi, aggiungi, Esegui, consulta, dovresti, sul tuo host).

No semantic drift found: every claim, caveat, quantity and conditional in the English survives intact (the ~150 tests, the three difficulty levels, the "Hard" variant removing import information so the LLM must infer them, the `"jupyter-ai<3"` pin and the "without it Ollama will not appear" warning, the "no API key needed for Ollama" note), the informal "tu" register holds throughout (Scopri, usa, Assicurati, Puoi, consulta — no Lei/consulti slips), and the sparse domain vocabulary is right (circuito parametrizzato, circuito di Bell, inferenza LLM su CPU, prompt di sistema, token). What a native technical editor would still change is stiffness and one consistency slip: line 21 stacks four genitives — "migliora le capacità di generazione del codice per Qiskit del modello `Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506`" — which no Italian writer would produce unrestructured; line 142 calques the English impersonal ("Questo processo potrebbe richiedere del tempo affinché Ollama legga il file...") instead of the natural "Ollama potrebbe impiegare del tempo per leggere..."; line 29 repeats "composti da ... ognuno dei quali è composto da". Release dates are translated in the model lists (line 389 "Rilasciato ottobre 2025") but left in English inside the benchmark table (line 418 "June 2025"), an inconsistency within the same page. Also line 27 adds "del settore" to "esperti", a specification the English does not make — harmless but unsupported.

examples.source: The `mistral-small-3.2-24b-qiskit` model improves the `Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506` model's code generation capabilities for Qiskit through extended pretraining and fine-tuning it on high-quality Qiskit data
examples.suggested: Il modello `mistral-small-3.2-24b-qiskit` potenzia la capacità del modello `Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506` di generare codice Qiskit, grazie a un pre-addestramento esteso e a un fine-tuning su dati Qiskit di alta qualità
examples.translation: Il modello `mistral-small-3.2-24b-qiskit` migliora le capacità di generazione del codice per Qiskit del modello `Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506` attraverso un pre-addestramento esteso e il fine-tuning su dati Qiskit di alta qualità
examples.why: Four stacked genitives ('del codice per Qiskit del modello') is a calque of the English possessive chain; the reader has to re-parse which model owns the capabilities. Restructuring with a verb phrase is what a native technical writer would do. Meaning is correct, so this is stylistic only.

examples.source: This process may take some time for Ollama to read the model file, initialize the model instance, and configure it according to the specifications provided.
examples.suggested: Ollama potrebbe impiegare un po' di tempo per leggere il file del modello, inizializzare l'istanza del modello e configurarla in base alle specifiche fornite.
examples.translation: Questo processo potrebbe richiedere del tempo affinché Ollama legga il file del modello, inizializzi l'istanza del modello e la configuri in base alle specifiche fornite.
examples.why: 'richiedere del tempo affinché Ollama legga' transposes the English 'take some time for X to do Y' construction literally; the purpose clause with 'affinché' + subjunctive is not how Italian expresses duration. Grammatical but audibly translated.

examples.source: Released June 2025 (model list) / June 2025 (benchmark table column 'Release date')
examples.suggested: giugno 2025 in both places
examples.translation: Rilasciato giugno 2025 (elenco) / June 2025 (tabella)
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: month names are localized in the two model lists (ottobre 2025, giugno 2025, febbraio 2025, novembre 2024) but left in English in the benchmark table rows, even though the table's own header row was translated ('Data di rilascio'). Not misleading, but visibly half-translated on the same page.

examples.source: we collaborated with Qiskit Advocates and experts to create the execution-based benchmarks
examples.suggested: abbiamo collaborato con i Qiskit Advocates ed esperti per creare i benchmark basati sull'esecuzione
examples.translation: abbiamo collaborato con i Qiskit Advocates ed esperti del settore per creare i benchmark basati sull'esecuzione
examples.why: 'del settore' is an added specification absent from the English, which leaves 'experts' unqualified. Too small to mislead a learner, but it is content the source does not license.

editor_note: One inverted negation makes the central no-go argument say the opposite of the English: "we can alternatively rule out the possibility of transmitting qubits using classical communication alone" becomes 「古典的通信だけでQubitを送ることの不可能性を排除することもできます」 — i.e. "we can rule out the IMPOSSIBILITY of sending qubits", which contradicts the immediately preceding 「答えはノーです」 and tells the learner the no-cloning argument establishes that classical-only transmission IS possible. It should read 「…を送ることが不可能であることを（別の方法で）示すこともできます」. Secondary, non-misleading problems: the keep-English glossary terms are applied inconsistently — "Qubit" vs lowercase "qubit" (e.g. 「qubit $\mathsf{A}$ と $\mathsf{B}$」 line ~16, 「qubit $\mathsf{B}$ はプロトコル実行前に」 line ~70, 「qubit $\mathsf{A}$ と $\mathsf{Q}$ は」 line ~221) and "Gate" vs 「ゲート」 vs 「制御NOT Gate」/「アダマールGate」/「$X$ ゲート」 in adjacent sentences; and one sentence has a broken topic/subject pairing (「アリスの測定はアリス自身が…情報を全く得られないことに注目してください」). Register is correct throughout: plain polite desu/masu, no keigo.

examples.source: This is not too difficult to prove mathematically using basic quantum information theory, but we can alternatively rule out the possibility of transmitting qubits using classical communication alone by thinking about the no-cloning theorem.
examples.suggested: …クローン禁止定理を考えることで、古典的通信だけでQubitを送ることは不可能だと示すこともできます。
examples.translation: これは基本的な量子情報理論を用いて数学的に証明することは難しくありませんが、クローン禁止定理を考えることで古典的通信だけでQubitを送ることの不可能性を排除することもできます。
examples.why: Inverted negation: 「不可能性を排除する」 = 'eliminate the impossibility', i.e. the opposite of 'rule out the possibility'. It flatly contradicts the preceding 「答えはノーです。古典的通信だけで量子情報を送信することは不可能です」 and would lead a learner to think the no-cloning argument supports classical-only qubit transmission.

examples.source: qubit A … qubit B … the qubits A and Q
examples.suggested: Use one casing consistently (e.g. always Qubit, or always 量子ビット) throughout the file.
examples.translation: アリスはQubit $\mathsf{A}$ を持ち… / 「qubit $\mathsf{A}$ と $\mathsf{B}$ を状態…に準備し」「qubit $\mathsf{B}$ はプロトコル実行前に」「qubit $\mathsf{A}$ と $\mathsf{Q}$ は」
examples.why: The kept-English term alternates between 'Qubit' and 'qubit' within the same paragraphs, and 'Gate' likewise alternates with 「ゲート」 (「制御NOT Gate」/「アダマールGate」/「量子Gate」 vs 「$X$ ゲート」「$Z$ ゲート」). Recognizable, not misleading, but an editor would unify it.

examples.source: Notice that Alice's measurements yield absolutely no information about the state α|0⟩ + β|1⟩.
examples.suggested: アリスの測定からは、状態 $\alpha \vert 0\rangle + \beta \vert 1\rangle$ に関する情報が一切得られないことに注目してください。
examples.translation: アリスの測定はアリス自身が $\alpha \vert 0\rangle + \beta \vert 1\rangle$ という状態に関する情報を全く得られないことに注目してください。
examples.why: The topic 「アリスの測定は」 does not pair with the embedded subject 「アリス自身が…得られない」; the sentence reads as ungrammatical MT rather than something a Japanese technical writer would produce, and it needlessly inserts 「アリス自身が」, which is not in the English.

examples.source: Indeed, it is reasonable to speculate that teleportation could one day become a standard way to communicate quantum information…
examples.suggested: 実際、テレポーテーションが…と推測するのは合理的です。
examples.translation: 確かに、テレポーテーションがいつか量子情報を通信する標準的な方法になるかもしれないと推測するのは合理的です。
examples.why: 「確かに」 reads as a concession ('admittedly / it is true that…'), whereas the English 'Indeed' here is an intensifier continuing the argument. The rhetorical direction of the paragraph is slightly flattened.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: every prose paragraph is semantically faithful (the PUB definition, the error-mitigation overhead sentence, and the "Sampler V2는 복원력 레벨 지정을 지원하지 않습니다" caveat all match the English exactly), and the 해요체 imperative convention holds throughout (참조하세요 / 알아보세요, no 하십시오체 or 드리 forms). The editorial defects are terminological. "circuit" is left in English as "Circuit" everywhere (QASM Circuit 만들기, 양자 Circuit, Circuit 오류, 매개변수화된 Circuit) even though the repo's own translation/glossary/ko.json sets preferred="회로" and explicitly lists "Circuit"/"Circuits" as leaked_en — and the same heading translates its sibling term ("양자 Circuit 생성 및 매개변수화된 게이트 추가"), so gate is Korean while circuit is not. "dynamical decoupling" is rendered "동적 분리" ("dynamic separation"), which back-translates wrongly; the field uses 동적 디커플링 or 동적 결합 해제. Both are recognizable in context (the DD heading sits directly above the `dynamical_decoupling` key), so this is polish, not a false concept.

examples.source: Create a QASM circuit / You need at least one circuit as the input to the Sampler primitive.
examples.suggested: QASM 회로 만들기 / Sampler Primitive의 입력으로 최소 하나의 회로가 필요합니다.
examples.translation: QASM Circuit 만들기 / Sampler Primitive에 대한 입력으로 최소한 하나의 Circuit이 필요합니다.
examples.why: The repo glossary (translation/glossary/ko.json) sets circuit→회로 and flags bare "Circuit" as an English leak. It is consistent within the file, so nothing is unidentifiable, but it clashes with the file's own handling of the neighbouring term: heading 3 reads "양자 Circuit 생성 및 매개변수화된 게이트 추가" — gate localized, circuit not.

examples.source: The following examples demonstrate the default options for dynamical decoupling and twirling. / ### Dynamical decoupling
examples.suggested: 다음 예제에서는 동적 디커플링(dynamical decoupling)과 트월링의 기본 옵션을 보여줍니다. / ### 동적 디커플링
examples.translation: 다음 예제에서는 동적 분리 및 트월링의 기본 옵션을 보여줍니다. / ### 동적 분리
examples.why: "분리" means separation/splitting, not decoupling; 동적 분리 is not the term a Korean quantum engineer would recognize as DD. The adjacent "트월링" is correctly transliterated, so the section mixes a transliteration with a loose literal calque. Recognizable from the `dynamical_decoupling` key below it, hence MINOR rather than a false concept.

examples.source: Practice with primitives by working through the Cost function lesson in IBM Quantum Learning.
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Learning의 [비용 함수 레슨]을 따라가며 Primitive를 직접 연습해 보세요.
examples.translation: IBM Quantum Learning의 [비용 함수 레슨]을 통해 Primitive 연습을 하세요.
examples.why: "…을 통해 … 연습을 하세요" is a stiff noun-plus-하다 construction typical of MT; a native technical writer would use the verbal form 연습해 보세요 and render "by working through" as 따라가며/실습하며. Meaning is intact — purely a fluency polish.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every number, condition and caveat (112 qubits, 84-qubit→120 population_size vs 56-qubit→40, "최소 population_size ~ 0.8 * n_qubits", Gurobi/random-baseline comparison) survives correctly, and register is consistent doc-standard 합니다체 with -하세요 imperatives. What a Korean editor would change is terminology hygiene: "qubit" and "circuit" are left in English mid-Korean-prose and with inconsistent casing — "해상도 Qubit … 112개의 Qubit" (l.57), "Circuit의 qubit 수" (l.120), "84-Qubit 문제" (l.122), "해상도 qubit, ansatz Circuit" (l.246) — where a native technical writer writes 큐비트 and 회로; "해상도 Qubit" for "resolution qubits" is also a display-resolution calque (분해능/정밀도 큐비트 is the intended sense). "Investment trajectories" is split within the file: 투자 경로 in the Overview and Function-description sections (ll.26, 30, 32) vs 투자 궤적 in section 5 (ll.167, 209). Two smaller flattenings: "sharply concentrated" loses 뚜렷하게/급격히 (l.244) and "demonstrably" becomes the odd 입증 가능하고 (l.240); l.116 is a noun-stacked calque of the English syntax.

examples.source: This case involves seven assets, four time steps, and four resolution qubits, resulting in a total requirement of 112 qubits.
examples.suggested: 이 경우 7개의 자산, 4개의 시간 단계, 4개의 분해능 큐비트를 포함하며, 총 112개의 큐비트가 필요합니다.
examples.translation: 이 경우 7개의 자산, 4개의 시간 단계, 4개의 해상도 Qubit를 포함하며, 총 112개의 Qubit가 필요합니다.
examples.why: 큐비트 is the settled Korean rendering; leaving the English word untranslated inside Korean prose — and with inconsistent casing across the file (Qubit at l.57/122, qubit at l.120/246, Circuit at l.120/122/246 where 회로 is standard) — reads as an untranslated glossary artifact. '해상도' is the image-resolution sense and is a calque here; the meaning is bits of precision (분해능/정밀도).

examples.source: investment trajectories
examples.suggested: pick one — 투자 궤적 throughout (or 투자 경로 throughout)
examples.why: The same concept, which is the function's central output, is named two different ways in the same document; a reader in section 5 cannot be sure 투자 궤적 is the 투자 경로 promised in the Overview.

examples.source: Optionally define specific requirements for the optimization process, including the selection of the optimizer and its parameters, as well as the specification of the primitive and its configurations.
examples.suggested: 필요하다면 옵티마이저와 파라미터를 선택하고 primitive와 그 설정을 지정하는 등 최적화 프로세스의 세부 요구 사항을 직접 정의할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: 선택적으로 옵티마이저와 그 파라미터의 선택, 그리고 primitive와 그 구성의 지정을 포함하여 최적화 프로세스에 대한 특정 요구 사항을 정의할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: '…의 선택, …의 지정을 포함하여' mirrors the English nominalizations one-for-one; Korean technical prose turns these into verbs (선택하고/지정하는). Grammatical but visibly translated.

examples.source: the cost distribution for our Variational Quantum Eigensolver (post-processed with SQD) approach is sharply concentrated at lower objective cost values
examples.suggested: …비용 분포는 낮은 목적 비용 값에 뚜렷하게 집중되어 있어
examples.translation: Variational Quantum Eigensolver(SQD로 후처리) 접근 방식의 비용 분포는 낮은 목적 비용 값에 집중되어 있어
examples.why: 'sharply' is dropped, so the contrast with the baseline's 'broader distribution' in the very next sentence is weaker than in the English — the figure's main teaching point is the sharpness of the peak.

examples.source: If the quantum algorithm demonstrably and consistently produces results with lower cost values, it indicates an effective optimization process.
examples.suggested: 양자 알고리즘이 명백하고 일관되게 더 낮은 비용의 결과를 낸다면, 최적화가 효과적으로 이루어지고 있다는 뜻입니다.
examples.translation: 양자 알고리즘이 입증 가능하고 일관되게 더 낮은 비용 값의 결과를 생성한다면, 이는 효과적인 최적화 프로세스를 나타냅니다.
examples.why: '입증 가능하고' reads as 'provable/verifiable', an adjective form awkwardly coordinated with the adverb 일관되게; 'demonstrably' here means 눈에 띄게/명백하게.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner, but a native technical editor would change several things. The most visible is that "circuit" is left as the capitalized English "Circuit" inside Malay prose in three places ("ensemble, Circuit yang berkaitan", "berbeza dari Circuit ke Circuit", "semua jenis Circuit") where standard Malay usage is "litar" — it reads as a glossary leak, not a deliberate keep-in-English convention (contrast the file's correct keeps of "twirling", "readout", "overhed"). Second, "measurement mitigation" becomes "pengurangan ukuran" ("size reduction") rather than "pengurangan ralat pengukuran", an imperfect but context-recoverable term. Third, the generic statistical "estimators" in the resilience-level-2 table row is rendered as the capitalized primitive name "Estimator", narrowing the claim to the Qiskit object. Remaining nits are translationese in the resilience-level paragraph: "cost/accuracy trade-off" → "pertukaran kos/ketepatan" (pertukaran = swap/exchange, not trade-off), the coined "mengabstrak", and the calqued discourse opener "Memandangkan ini" for "Given this".

examples.source: processing the outputs from a collection, or ensemble, of related circuits
examples.suggested: memproses output daripada koleksi, atau ensemble, litar yang berkaitan
examples.translation: memproses output daripada koleksi, atau ensemble, Circuit yang berkaitan
examples.why: "circuit" is a term Malay technical writing translates (litar); leaving the capitalized English noun inside Malay prose reads as an untranslated glossary leak. It recurs at line 61 ("berbeza dari Circuit ke Circuit") and line 103 ("semua jenis Circuit"), so the file is consistent in the leak but inconsistent with normal Malay domain usage.

examples.source: you could set the resilience level to 1, but then turn off measurement mitigation
examples.suggested: ...tetapi kemudian mematikan pengurangan ralat pengukuran
examples.translation: anda boleh menetapkan tahap daya tahan ke 1, tetapi kemudian mematikan pengurangan ukuran
examples.why: "pengurangan ukuran" most naturally reads as "size reduction"; "ukuran" is size, not the act of measuring. The intended concept is measurement-error mitigation, which the file itself elsewhere handles with "pengukuran" (line 55) and "ralat readout". Recoverable from context, hence minor, but a native editor would fix it.

examples.source: Typically reduces bias in estimators, but is not guaranteed to be zero-bias.
examples.suggested: Biasanya mengurangkan bias dalam penganggar, tetapi tidak dijamin bebas bias.
examples.translation: Biasanya mengurangkan berat sebelah dalam Estimator, tetapi tidak dijamin bebas-berat sebelah.
examples.why: English "estimators" here means statistical estimators (the estimates produced), but the capitalized "Estimator" is used everywhere else in this file for the Qiskit primitive, so the sentence narrows to a claim about the primitive object. Also "berat sebelah" is the social sense of bias; statistical bias is normally "bias" or "pincang" in Malay technical prose.

examples.source: Resilience levels can be used to configure the cost/accuracy trade-off ... The resilience level abstracts the detailed choice of noise management method
examples.suggested: ...mengkonfigurasi pertimbangan (timbal balik) kos–ketepatan ... Tahap daya tahan menyembunyikan butiran pemilihan kaedah pengurusan hingar
examples.translation: ...mengkonfigurasi pertukaran kos/ketepatan ... Tahap daya tahan mengabstrak pilihan terperinci kaedah pengurusan hingar
examples.why: "pertukaran" means swap/exchange and does not carry the trade-off sense; "mengabstrak" is a coined calque of "abstracts" that no Malay technical writer would use. Both are grammatical but read as machine output rather than authored prose.

examples.source: Given this, each level corresponds to a method or methods with increasing level of quantum sampling overhead
examples.suggested: Oleh itu, setiap tahap sepadan dengan satu atau lebih kaedah yang mempunyai overhed pensampelan kuantum yang semakin meningkat
examples.translation: Memandangkan ini, setiap tahap sepadan dengan kaedah atau kaedah-kaedah dengan tahap overhed pensampelan kuantum yang semakin meningkat
examples.why: "Memandangkan ini" is a literal transfer of "Given this" and is not idiomatic as a discourse connector; "kaedah atau kaedah-kaedah" mechanically mirrors the English singular/plural pair instead of the natural "satu atau lebih kaedah". Minor stiffness in the paragraph that carries the guide's central explanation.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, the 84-qubit/120 vs 56-qubit/40 population_size example and the "lowest to highest objective function value" ordering both match the English exactly, and domain terms are handled sensibly (qubit, ansatz, VQE/QUBO, Ising Hamiltonian kept in English; "hingar" used consistently for noise in "peka hingar" / "garis dasar berhingar"). What a native technical editor would change: the English word "Circuit" is left untranslated and oddly capitalized mid-sentence three times ("bilangan qubit dalam Circuit", "pelaksanaan Circuit", "Circuit ansatz") where Malay uses "litar"; "sharply concentrated" is rendered "terumpu rapat", where "terumpu" is a misspelling of "tertumpu"; "blue solid line" becomes "garisan pepejal biru", a literal calque using "pepejal" (solid as in solid matter) instead of "garis penuh/solid". Also "post-processing" is rendered as "pemprosesan semula"/"diproses semula" ("re-processing") rather than "pasca-pemprosesan", and "Restriction Deviation" as "Penyelewengan Kekangan" ("penyelewengan" carries a misappropriation sense; "sisihan"/"penyimpangan" is the statistical term). None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: the number of qubits in the circuit … requires more circuit executions … ansatz circuits
examples.suggested: bilangan qubit dalam litar … memerlukan lebih banyak pelaksanaan litar … litar ansatz
examples.translation: bilangan qubit dalam Circuit … memerlukan lebih banyak pelaksanaan Circuit … Circuit ansatz
examples.why: "Circuit" is left in English and capitalized mid-sentence, reading as an unresolved glossary token; Malay technical writing uses "litar" (and "litar" is not otherwise avoided in this file).

examples.source: is sharply concentrated at lower objective cost values
examples.suggested: tertumpu rapat pada nilai kos objektif yang lebih rendah
examples.translation: terumpu rapat pada nilai kos objektif yang lebih rendah
examples.why: "terumpu" is not a Malay word — the intended form is "tertumpu"; a native writer would not leave this.

examples.source: As shown in the figure (blue solid line)
examples.suggested: Seperti yang ditunjukkan dalam rajah (garis penuh biru)
examples.translation: Seperti yang ditunjukkan dalam rajah (garisan pepejal biru)
examples.why: "pepejal" means solid as in a solid substance/state of matter, not an unbroken line; it is a literal calque that a Malay engineer would never write in a figure legend.

examples.source: finally, the results are post-processed … The system also includes a noise-aware (SQD-based) post-processing
examples.suggested: akhirnya, keputusan melalui pasca-pemprosesan … pasca-pemprosesan yang peka hingar (berasaskan SQD)
examples.translation: akhirnya, keputusan diproses semula … pemprosesan semula yang peka hingar (berasaskan SQD)
examples.why: "diproses semula"/"pemprosesan semula" means re-processed (doing it again), losing the "after the main computation" sense of post-processing; "pasca-pemprosesan" is the established Malay term.

examples.source: Optionally define specific requirements for the optimization process
examples.suggested: Anda boleh mentakrifkan keperluan khusus untuk proses pengoptimuman (pilihan)
examples.translation: Secara pilihan takrifkan keperluan khusus untuk proses pengoptimuman
examples.why: "Secara pilihan takrifkan" is a word-order calque of English "Optionally define"; Malay puts the optionality on the clause, not as a fronted adverb before the imperative.

editor_note: No semantic drift, inversion or quantity error — every number, claim and caveat matches the English, and the informal "ty" register holds throughout ("przeprowadzimy cię", "zapisałeś już swoje dane"). The defects are terminological. (1) "circuit" is rendered two ways in the same file: raw untranslated "Circuit" in the descriptive prose (5x, lines 30/36/38 — "wysoce skompresowane Circuit", "głębokością Circuit", "Circuit o mniejszej głębokości") but correctly as "obwód/obwodu/obwodów" in the transpilation section (lines 133/135); the same leak hits "Gate" ("Ze względu na mniejszą liczbę Gate", line 38, sitting next to correct "bramek splątujących" in the very same paragraph), "Qubit" capitalized as a proper noun everywhere instead of Polish "kubit", and "Backend" (line 295). (2) The false friend "term" → "termin" appears twice for mathematical terms: "wprowadzenie terminów kontradiabatycznych" (line 30, should be "członów/wyrazów kontradiabatycznych") and "lokalność terminów w funkcji celu" (line 57) — "termin" in Polish means terminology or deadline, never a summand, so the central mechanism sentence of the algorithm reads as nonsense to a Polish physicist. (3) "distribution of states" → "dystrybucja stanów" (3x, lines 40/42) instead of the conventional "rozkład stanów" — "dystrybucja" is distribution as in distributing goods. Also "benchmark" is split between "testy porównawcze" and "instancje benchmarkowe", which desynchronizes the cross-reference label at line 79 from the actual heading at line 274.

examples.source: This compression is achieved by introducing counterdiabatic terms into the underlying time evolution of the quantum system.
examples.suggested: ... poprzez wprowadzenie członów kontradiabatycznych do bazowej ewolucji czasowej układu kwantowego.
examples.translation: Kompresja ta jest osiągana poprzez wprowadzenie terminów kontradiabatycznych do bazowej ewolucji czasowej układu kwantowego.
examples.why: Classic false friend: Polish "termin" means a piece of terminology or a deadline, never a mathematical term/summand. The correct rendering is "człon" (or "wyraz"). This is the sentence that explains the core mechanism of bf-DCQO, so the reader is left unable to picture what is actually added to the Hamiltonian. Same error at line 57: "gęstość i lokalność terminów w funkcji celu" → "gęstość i lokalność członów w funkcji celu".

examples.source: It solves optimization problems by running highly-compressed quantum circuits on quantum hardware. / ... results in quantum circuits with shorter depth and fewer entangling gates. / Because of the smaller number of gates ...
examples.suggested: ... uruchamiając wysoce skompresowane obwody kwantowe na sprzęcie kwantowym. / ... skutkuje obwodami o mniejszej głębokości i mniejszej liczbie bramek splątujących. / Ze względu na mniejszą liczbę bramek ...
examples.translation: Rozwiązuje problemy optymalizacyjne, uruchamiając wysoce skompresowane Circuit na sprzęcie kwantowym. / ... skutkuje Circuit o mniejszej głębokości i mniejszej liczbie bramek splątujących. / Ze względu na mniejszą liczbę Gate ...
examples.why: Glossary leak: the English nouns "Circuit" and "Gate" are dropped uninflected into Polish sentences, which is ungrammatical (Polish needs case endings) and inconsistent — the same file correctly writes "obwodu/obwód/obwodów" at lines 133–135 and "bramek splątujących" in the same paragraph as "Gate". "Qubit" is likewise capitalized as a brand name throughout ("do 156 Qubitów", "z liczbą Qubitów") where Polish uses lowercase "kubit".

examples.source: After each iteration of the algorithm, the distribution of states is measured. The obtained distribution is used to calculate a so-called bias-field. / After measuring the distribution of states, a local search is performed.
examples.suggested: Po każdej iteracji algorytmu mierzony jest rozkład stanów. Uzyskany rozkład służy do obliczenia tzw. pola biasu. / Po zmierzeniu rozkładu stanów ...
examples.translation: Po każdej iteracji algorytmu mierzona jest dystrybucja stanów. Uzyskana dystrybucja służy do obliczenia tzw. pola biasu. / Po zmierzeniu dystrybucji stanów wykonywane jest lokalne przeszukiwanie.
examples.why: In Polish a probability distribution is "rozkład"; "dystrybucja" means distribution in the logistics/software-delivery sense. Recognizable but wrong for the domain, and used consistently wrongly three times.

examples.source: Qiskit Functions are an experimental feature available only to IBM Quantum Premium Plan, Flex Plan, and On-Prem ... users.
examples.suggested: Qiskit Functions to funkcjonalność eksperymentalna, dostępna wyłącznie dla użytkowników planów IBM Quantum® Premium Plan, Flex Plan i On-Prem (przez IBM Quantum Platform API).
examples.translation: Funkcje Qiskit to funkcja eksperymentalna dostępna wyłącznie dla użytkowników planów IBM Quantum® Premium Plan, Flex Plan i On-Prem (przez IBM Quantum Platform API).
examples.why: "Funkcje ... to funkcja" is a clumsy plural-to-singular collision that no native technical writer would leave: the product name "Qiskit Functions" (kept in English everywhere else in the file, e.g. "dostępu do Optimizera przez Qiskit Functions") is here half-translated, and "feature" is better as "funkcjonalność" to avoid echoing "funkcja".

examples.source: An example to run these instances can be found in [Example 3: Benchmark instances](#example-3-benchmark-instances). / ## Example 3: Benchmark instances
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering — either "Instancje testów porównawczych" or "Instancje benchmarkowe" — and use it in both the heading and the cross-reference label.
examples.translation: ... można znaleźć w [Przykładzie 3: Instancje testów porównawczych](#example-3-benchmark-instances). / ## Przykład 3: Instancje benchmarkowe
examples.why: "Benchmark" is split across the file between "testy porównawcze" (headings/prose, lines 55, 57, 79) and "benchmarkowe/benchmarku" (lines 274, 275, 283, 295). The split desynchronizes the in-page link text at line 79 from the heading it points at, so a reader who follows it lands on a section with a different name.

editor_note: Meaning is broadly faithful and the register is correctly informal ("Jeśli ten materiał był dla ciebie interesujący"), but a native technical editor would rewrite a lot. Glossary-protected English nouns are left capitalized and undeclined mid-sentence, which breaks Polish grammar: "każdy Qubit", "pierwszego Qubitu", "wybranego Backend", "na podstawie Backend", "model szumu Backend", "kafelkujemy Backend" — the conventional Polish is lowercase "kubit/kubitu" and a declined "backendu". Terminology is imperfect in three places: "parameter sweep" is rendered throughout as "przestrzeń parametrów" (= parameter *space*, a different concept — "Uruchamiamy przestrzeń parametrów z EstimatorV2" reads as "we run the parameter space"); "transpiled circuit" becomes "stransponowanym obwodzie" (= *transposed*, a false friend, and inconsistent with the correct "transpilujemy" one paragraph earlier); and "sub-circuit" becomes "podukład CHSH" while "circuit" is "obwód" everywhere else and "układ" is simultaneously used for "layout". Additionally the Background strengthens the English claim — "is used to experimentally test Bell's theorem" becomes "służy do eksperymentalnego udowodnienia twierdzenia Bella" (to *prove*) — plus calques "w kategoriach $A$, $a$..." ("in terms of"), "menedżer przejść był ćwiczony od początku do końca" ("exercised end-to-end"), "prostopadłych bazach" for orthogonal bases, undeclined "pary Bell"/"granicy Tsirelson" (should be "pary Bella"/"granicy Tsirelsona"), and the untranslated fragment "obwód Bell-state CHSH" alongside the correct "stan Bella" elsewhere.

examples.source: How to compute expectation values of multiple observables on a parameter sweep in a single call … / Run the parameter sweep with `EstimatorV2` in `aer_sim` mode.
examples.suggested: …dla przemiatanego parametru / Wykonujemy przemiatanie parametru za pomocą `EstimatorV2` w trybie `aer_sim`.
examples.translation: Jak obliczać wartości oczekiwane wielu obserwabli na przestrzeni parametrów w jednym wywołaniu … / Uruchamiamy przestrzeń parametrów z `EstimatorV2` w trybie `aer_sim`.
examples.why: "parameter sweep" is consistently rendered as "przestrzeń parametrów" = parameter *space*, a distinct concept. "Uruchamiamy przestrzeń parametrów" literally says "we run the parameter space", which no Polish quantum engineer would write; the tutorial sweeps one angle over 21 values, it does not run a space.

examples.source: We also transform the observables to match the transpiled circuit's qubit layout using `SparsePauliOp.apply_layout`.
examples.suggested: …do układu kubitów w obwodzie po transpilacji (stranspilowanym), używając…
examples.translation: Przekształcamy też obserwable tak, aby pasowały do układu Qubitów w stransponowanym obwodzie, używając `SparsePauliOp.apply_layout`.
examples.why: "stransponowany" means *transposed* (matrix/musical transposition), not *transpiled* — a classic false friend, and inconsistent with the correct verb "transpilujemy" used in the immediately preceding paragraph.

examples.source: The CHSH inequality … is used to experimentally test Bell's theorem (1969).
examples.suggested: … służy do eksperymentalnego testowania (sprawdzania) twierdzenia Bella (1969).
examples.translation: Nierówność CHSH … służy do eksperymentalnego udowodnienia twierdzenia Bella (1969).
examples.why: "udowodnienia" = *to prove*, strengthening the English "test". Bell's theorem is a mathematical result that experiments test, not prove; the English deliberately avoids this wording and the Polish asserts something stronger than the source.

examples.source: …inherits the noise model and coupling map of the backend you selected… / We build the `AerSimulator` from the backend…
examples.suggested: …wybranego backendu… / Budujemy `AerSimulator` na podstawie backendu…
examples.translation: …dziedziczący model szumu i mapę sprzężeń wybranego Backend… / Budujemy `AerSimulator` na podstawie Backend…
examples.why: "Backend" (and likewise "Qubit/Qubitu/Qubitów") stays capitalized and undeclined, so the noun phrases are ungrammatical in Polish — "wybranego Backend" has no case agreement. It reads as a glossary-protection artifact, not as prose a Polish author wrote.

examples.source: …and transpile against the simulator's target so the same pass manager is exercised end-to-end.
examples.suggested: …aby ten sam pass manager (menedżer przebiegów) został wykorzystany na całej ścieżce.
examples.translation: …i transpilujemy względem celu symulatora, tak aby ten sam menedżer przejść był ćwiczony od początku do końca.
examples.why: "był ćwiczony" is a literal calque of "exercised" — in Polish it means physically trained/drilled, which is nonsense for a pass manager; "menedżer przejść" also over-translates a term the Polish Qiskit community normally keeps as "pass manager".

examples.source: Expanding $S_1$ in terms of $A$, $a$, $B$, and $b$ gives:
examples.suggested: Wyrażając $S_1$ przez $A$, $a$, $B$ i $b$, otrzymujemy:
examples.translation: Rozwijając $S_1$ w kategoriach $A$, $a$, $B$ i $b$, otrzymujemy:
examples.why: "w kategoriach" is a well-known Anglicism for "in terms of"; Polish mathematical prose says "wyrażając przez" or "względem". Grammatical, but immediately marks the text as translated.

editor_note: Faithful, natural pt-BR overall — informal "você" holds throughout, and core terms are correct and consistent (qubit → "qubit", string de Pauli, matriz densa, observáveis, combinação linear, adjunto, "(anti)comuta"). Three things a native technical editor would change: (1) "dot product" is rendered "produto escalar" (line ~133), which in Portuguese means the *inner/scalar* product and suggests a numeric result, whereas `Pauli.dot` is operator composition returning another `Pauli` — "produto (dot)" or "produto matricial" is the right rendering; (2) "single-qubit operator" is silently changed to "operador de subsistema único" (line ~202) — the substitution is arguably more accurate physics, but it is not what the English says and diverges from the source claim; (3) "which is the reverse of the shape" → "que é o inverso da forma" (line ~165) reads as the mathematical *inverse* rather than reversed order — "a ordem inversa da forma" is clearer. Also cosmetic: "M-Qubit e N-Qubit" is capitalized mid-sentence (line ~189) where the English has lowercase "M-qubit and N-qubit", and "cobertura mais aprofundada" (line ~258) is a mild calque of "in-depth coverage". None of these would lead a learner to a false concept.

examples.source: computing the dot product with another `Pauli`
examples.suggested: calcular o produto (dot) com outro `Pauli`
examples.translation: calcular o produto escalar com outro `Pauli`
examples.why: "produto escalar" is the Portuguese term for the inner/scalar product, which yields a number; Qiskit's `Pauli.dot` is operator composition and returns a `Pauli`. Recognizable but the wrong domain term here.

examples.source: then it will be stored as a single-qubit operator
examples.suggested: ela será armazenada como um operador de um único qubit
examples.translation: ela será armazenada como um operador de subsistema único
examples.why: The English says "single-qubit operator"; the translation substitutes "single-subsystem". Not misleading (it matches the (6,) output better than the English does), but it is an unannounced change of the source claim.

examples.source: which is the reverse of the shape of the underlying matrix
examples.suggested: que é a ordem inversa da forma da matriz subjacente
examples.translation: que é o inverso da forma da matriz subjacente
examples.why: "o inverso" reads as the mathematical inverse; the English means the ordering is reversed. A native technical writer would write "a ordem inversa".

examples.source: the input and output dimensions are automatically assumed to be M-qubit and N-qubit
examples.suggested: ... assumidas como M-qubit e N-qubit
examples.translation: as dimensões de entrada e saída são automaticamente assumidas como M-Qubit e N-Qubit
