examples.why: Mid-sentence capitalization of "Qubit" is inconsistent with the lowercase "qubits" used everywhere else in the file (lines 136, 138, 202) and with the English source.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no dropped caveats, and the informal "você" register holds ("Você pode então selecionar a QPU que deseja usar", "primeiro você precisa inicializar sua conta"). The real defect is a glossary leak in the opening paragraph: "circuit" is left as the English plural "Circuits" with a capital C ("um ou mais Circuits quânticos", "Circuits dinâmicos e Circuits parametrizados"), while the rest of the file correctly uses "circuito/circuitos" ("Você precisa de pelo menos um circuito", "O circuito e o observável"), so the same concept is split two ways within one file. The same capitalized-English-noun leak hits "Backend" ("ao solicitar um Backend de uma instância") and "Session" in step 3, where the list of execution modes is rendered half-translated, half-not: "os modos de execução em lote, Session e job" — batch is translated, session and job are not. "Open Plan" is also over-translated to "Plano Aberto", which is an IBM plan name users see in English in the console. None of this misleads; a native technical editor would simply normalize it.

examples.source: The Sampler's core task is sampling the output register from the execution of one or more quantum circuits. Dynamic circuits and parameterized circuits are accepted as input (if parametrized circuits are submitted, ...)
examples.suggested: ... de um ou mais circuitos quânticos. [Circuitos dinâmicos] e circuitos parametrizados são aceitos como entrada (se circuitos parametrizados forem enviados, ...)
examples.translation: A tarefa principal do Sampler é amostrar o registrador de saída a partir da execução de um ou mais Circuits quânticos. [Circuits dinâmicos] e Circuits parametrizados são aceitos como entrada (se Circuits parametrizados forem enviados, ...)
examples.why: Glossary leak: the English plural noun "Circuits" is kept and capitalized four times in the lead paragraph, while the rest of the file uses the correct Portuguese "circuito/circuitos" (lines 72, 84, 110). Same concept, two renderings in one file; "Circuits quânticos" is also ungrammatical as Portuguese (English plural + Portuguese adjective).

examples.source: Possible values are `batch`, `session`, or `backend` objects for batch, session, and job execution mode, respectively. ... Note that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs.
examples.suggested: ... para os modos de execução em lote (batch), sessão e job, respectivamente. ... Note que usuários do Open Plan não podem enviar jobs de sessão.
examples.translation: Os valores possíveis são objetos `batch`, `session` ou `backend` para os modos de execução em lote, Session e job, respectivamente. ... Note que usuários do Plano Aberto não podem enviar jobs de Session.
examples.why: The three mode names are handled three different ways in one sentence: "batch" translated to "em lote", "session" left as capitalized English "Session", "job" left lowercase English. Either translate all three or keep all three; the mixture reads as an unfinished glossary pass. "Plano Aberto" also over-translates an IBM plan name the learner sees as "Open Plan" in the console.

examples.source: set `use_fractional_gates=True` when requesting a backend from a `QiskitRuntimeService` instance
examples.suggested: defina `use_fractional_gates=True` ao solicitar um backend de uma instância `QiskitRuntimeService`
examples.translation: defina `use_fractional_gates=True` ao solicitar um Backend de uma instância `QiskitRuntimeService`
examples.why: "Backend" is capitalized mid-sentence as if it were a proper noun/class name, but here it refers to the common noun. Keeping "backend" in English is the right call for pt; the capital B is a leftover glossary marker, not a native writer's choice.

examples.source: The circuit and observable need to be transformed to only use instructions supported by the QPU (referred to as *instruction set architecture (ISA)* circuits). Use the transpiler to do this.
examples.suggested: ... (chamados de circuitos *ISA*, de arquitetura de conjunto de instruções). Use o transpilador para isso.
examples.translation: O circuito e o observável precisam ser transformados para usar apenas instruções suportadas pela QPU (referidos como circuitos de *arquitetura de conjunto de instruções (ISA)*). Use o Transpiler para isso.
examples.why: Minor stiffness plus one more capitalization leak: "o Transpiler" is capitalized English here, while the Next-steps list uses the Portuguese verb "transpilar"/"Transpilar" (line 147). Defensible either way, but pick one form for the tool across the file.

editor_note: Two entire explanatory paragraphs are missing from the "Exemplu de configurare personalizată" section: the EN "**Seed optimization**: Note that `seed_transpiler` is set to `None` by default…" and "**Transpilation level performance**: Increasing the number of `max_trials`…" paragraphs (EN lines 128 and 130). The RO file jumps straight from the `custom_options` code block (line 125) to "## Example 1". This drops the only statement of the default (`seed_transpiler=None`) and the entire `max_trials` / transpilation-time trade-off caveat, so a Romanian learner who sees `"seed_transpiler": 42` in the sample config is left believing 42 is the norm and never learns that leaving it unset triggers the automatic multi-seed depth search — a dropped caveat that misleads. Separately, terminology for "gate" is broken and split within two adjacent sentences: "Gate-uri de entanglare" (line 32/34) alongside "poartă-uri" (line 34), which is not a Romanian word at all (plural of *poartă* is *porți*); "Circuit-ului"/"circuit-uri" and "Backend-ul" carry the same mid-sentence capitalized-English artifact. Also "ground state" is rendered as "starea de bază" rather than the standard "starea fundamentală" (risking confusion with *basis state*), the heading "## Example 1: Funcție de cost simplă" was left in English while Examples 2 and 3 are "Exemplul 2/3", and `®` was moved off IBM onto the wrong noun ("calculatoarele® cuantice IBM").

examples.source: **Seed optimization**: Note that `seed_transpiler` is set to `None` by default. This enables the transpiler's automatic optimization process. When `None`, the system will start a trial with multiple seeds and select the one that produces the best circuit depth, leveraging the full power of the `max_trials` parameter for each transpilation level.
examples.suggested: **Optimizarea seed-ului**: Reține că `seed_transpiler` este setat implicit la `None`. Acest lucru activează procesul automat de optimizare al transpilatorului. Când este `None`, sistemul pornește o serie de încercări cu mai multe seed-uri și îl selectează pe cel care produce cea mai bună adâncime a circuitului, folosind la maximum parametrul `max_trials` pentru fiecare nivel de transpilare.
examples.translation: (omitted entirely — the RO file goes from the closing `}` of the code block straight to `## Example 1`)
examples.why: A dropped caveat. The sample config shows `"seed_transpiler": 42`; without this note the Romanian reader never learns the parameter's default is `None` nor that `None` is what enables the automatic best-depth search, so the example is read as prescriptive rather than as an override.

examples.source: **Transpilation level performance**: Increasing the number of `max_trials` with higher values for `transpilation_level` will unavoidably increase the transpilation time, but it might not always change the final circuit … the difference between 10 trials (level 1) and 50 trials (level 5) can be dramatic, so exploring these parameters might be the key to successfully finding a solution.
examples.suggested: **Performanța nivelului de transpilare**: Creșterea numărului de `max_trials` împreună cu valori mai mari pentru `transpilation_level` va mări inevitabil timpul de transpilare, dar s-ar putea să nu schimbe întotdeauna circuitul final — depinde puternic de structura și complexitatea circuitului. Totuși, pentru unele circuite/probleme, diferența dintre 10 încercări (nivelul 1) și 50 de încercări (nivelul 5) poate fi dramatică, așa că explorarea acestor parametri poate fi cheia găsirii unei soluții.
examples.translation: (omitted entirely)
examples.why: The whole cost/benefit caveat about `max_trials` vs transpilation time is gone, including the practical hint that tuning these parameters may be what makes a problem solvable. Pedagogically the RO section is now a bare code block with no guidance.

examples.source: Because of the smaller number of gates, fewer errors occur during the circuit execution on hardware.
examples.suggested: Datorită numărului mai mic de porți, apar mai puține erori în timpul execuției circuitului pe hardware.
examples.translation: Datorită numărului mai mic de poartă-uri, apar mai puține erori în timpul execuției Circuit-ului pe hardware.
examples.why: "poartă-uri" is a malformed hybrid that does not exist in Romanian (the plural of *poartă* is *porți*), and it sits one sentence after "Gate-uri de entanglare" — the same concept rendered two different broken ways within one paragraph. "Circuit-ului"/"circuit-uri" and "Backend-ul" (line 286) show the same capitalized-English-stem artifact.

examples.source: the problem solution is encoded in the ground state of the quantum system … AR=100% means that the ground state of the problem has been obtained.
examples.suggested: …codificată în starea fundamentală a sistemului cuantic … s-a obținut starea fundamentală a problemei.
examples.translation: soluția problemei este codificată în starea de bază a sistemului cuantic … AR=100% înseamnă că s-a obținut starea de bază a problemei.
examples.why: "stare de bază" is a calque; the established Romanian physics term for *ground state* is "stare fundamentală". As written it can be misread as *basis state* (starea bazei), a distinct concept in the same domain. Used consistently, so recognizable — but a native technical editor would change all three occurrences.

examples.source: where $C$ is the objective function, $C_{min}$, $C_{max}$ are its minimum and maximum values, and $C^{*}$ is the cost of the best solution found, respectively.
examples.suggested: …iar $C^{*}$ este costul celei mai bune soluții găsite.
examples.translation: unde $C$ este funcția obiectiv, $C_{min}$, $C_{max}$ sunt valorile sale minime și maxime, iar $C^{*}$ este costul celei mai bune soluții găsite, respectiv.
examples.why: Trailing "respectiv" is a direct calque of English "respectively", which Romanian does not place sentence-finally; it reads as an untranslated leftover. Same paragraph-level stiffness appears at line 32 with "infamului algoritm QAOA" — Romanian *infam* means vile/despicable, a much stronger negative than the EN "infamous" (here meaning notorious/well-known).

examples.source: ## Example 1: Simple cost function … using IBM® quantum computers
examples.suggested: ## Exemplul 1: Funcție de cost simplă … folosind calculatoarele cuantice IBM®
examples.translation: ## Example 1: Funcție de cost simplă … folosind calculatoarele® cuantice IBM
examples.why: "Example 1" was left in English while the parallel headings at lines 194 and 264 are "Exemplul 2" / "Exemplul 3" — an inconsistency visible in the table of contents. Separately the registered-trademark mark migrated off "IBM" onto "calculatoarele", so the RO page trademarks the word "computers". Informal *tu* register otherwise holds correctly throughout (poți, reține, consultă, autentifică-te).

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout (promise, both cases, the null-space/Gaussian-elimination post-processing, the 1 - 2^-r bound and the classical 2^(n/2-1)-1 lower bound all land correctly), and the informal "tu" register holds ("Observă că…", "imaginează-ți pentru o clipă"). The defects are terminological and stylistic, concentrated in the "Descrierea algoritmului" section: "gate" is rendered three ways in three consecutive sentences — the non-word "poartă-uri Hadamard" (a mangled singular "poartă" + plural "-uri"; correct is "porți Hadamard", which the file itself uses correctly nine lines later), the untranslated "Gate-ul de interogare" (elsewhere the domain term is consistently "poartă"), plus stray capitalised/hyphenated "Qubiți" and "Circuit-ului" where the rest of the file writes "qubiți" and "circuitului". Separately, "two-to-one" is split between "doi-la-unu" (Cazul 2, and the eight-value example) and "două-la-unu" (Cazul 2 of the Analiză section), the English word "proof" is left untranslated in "Acesta nu este un proof formal" (should be "o demonstrație formală"), and there are two grammar slips: "iar putem folosi acele dovezi" (should be "și putem folosi") and "mai puțin de … interogări / … șiruri" (countables require "mai puține de"). None of this misleads a learner, but a native technical editor would change all of it.

examples.source: there are $n$ qubits on the top that are acted upon by Hadamard gates and $m$ qubits on the bottom that go directly into the query gate ... the bottom $m$ qubits all go into the query gate
examples.suggested: există $n$ qubiți în partea de sus asupra cărora acționează porți Hadamard și $m$ qubiți în partea de jos care intră direct în poarta de interogare ... cei $m$ qubiți din partea de jos intră în poarta de interogare
examples.translation: există $n$ Qubiți în partea de sus care sunt acționați de poartă-uri Hadamard și $m$ Qubiți în partea de jos care intră direct în Gate-ul de interogare ... cei $m$ Qubiți din partea de jos intră în Gate-ul de interogare
examples.why: "poartă-uri" is not a Romanian word (singular "poartă" with a plural suffix glued on); the correct plural "porți Hadamard" is used correctly a few lines later in the Analiză section. "Gate-ul de interogare" leaves the term in English inside Romanian prose, and "Qubiți" is capitalised mid-sentence against the file's own "qubiți". Three renderings of one term in three sentences.

examples.source: after the behavior of the circuit is analyzed
examples.suggested: după ce comportamentul circuitului este analizat
examples.translation: după ce comportamentul Circuit-ului este analizat
examples.why: Same leak pattern: the common noun "circuit" is capitalised and hyphenated as if it were an English loan, while the rest of the file writes "circuitul / circuitului" normally (e.g. "rulăm circuitul cuantic", "fiecare execuție a circuitului").

examples.source: $f$ is *two-to-one* ... so this is a two-to-one function ... In this case $f$ is two-to-one
examples.suggested: pick one form and use it in all three places (e.g. *doi-la-unu* throughout)
examples.translation: $f$ este *doi-la-unu* ... aceasta este o funcție doi-la-unu ... În acest caz $f$ este două-la-unu
examples.why: The same defined term appears as "doi-la-unu" where it is introduced and italicised, then as "două-la-unu" in the Analiză section. Recognisable, but a learner tracking the defined term sees two spellings of it.

examples.source: This isn't a formal proof, it's just the basic idea.
examples.suggested: Aceasta nu este o demonstrație formală, este doar ideea de bază.
examples.translation: Acesta nu este un proof formal, este doar ideea de bază.
examples.why: The English word "proof" is left untranslated in the middle of a Romanian sentence; the Romanian term is "demonstrație" (and the gender then requires "Aceasta ... o demonstrație formală"). No native technical writer would leave this.

examples.source: each execution of the circuit provides us with statistical evidence concerning $s,$ and we can use that evidence to find $s$
examples.suggested: ... cu privire la $s,$ și putem folosi acele dovezi pentru a găsi $s$
examples.translation: fiecare execuție a circuitului ne oferă dovezi statistice cu privire la $s,$ iar putem folosi acele dovezi pentru a găsi $s$
examples.why: "iar putem" is ungrammatical — the coordinating "iar" cannot directly precede a verb here; a plain "și" is required. Reads as an unrevised literal rendering of the English "and".

examples.source: We'll unpack the promise to better understand what it says momentarily, but first let's be clear that ...
examples.suggested: Vom analiza imediat promisiunea, pentru a înțelege mai bine ce spune, dar mai întâi să fie clar că ...
examples.translation: Vom desface promisiunea pentru a înțelege mai bine ce spune imediat, dar mai întâi să fie clar că ...
examples.why: Word-for-word ordering leaves "imediat" stranded at the end, where it attaches to "ce spune" ("what it says immediately") rather than to the act of unpacking. "Desface promisiunea" is also a literal calque of "unpack"; "analizăm/detaliem promisiunea" is the natural technical phrasing.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the shots precedence list, the twirling failure caveat ("งานจะล้มเหลวถ้า twirling เปิดใช้งานและผลคูณของ num_randomizations และ shots_per_randomization มีค่าน้อยกว่าค่า shots"), and the run()/default_shots override are all rendered correctly, and register is consistently casual with no ครับ/ค่ะ. What a native editor would change: "qubit" is split within the file between Latin-script "Qubit" (execution.init_qubits: "รีเซ็ต Qubit ให้กลับสู่สถานะพื้นฐาน") and the nonstandard transliteration "ควิบิต" (simulator.coupling_map: "ปฏิสัมพันธ์สองควิบิต") — the conventional Thai form is "คิวบิต", and one file should pick one. In simulator.noise_model, "or its representation" becomes "หรือการแสดงผลของมัน", where การแสดงผล means on-screen display/output rather than a serialized representation (การแสดงแทน / รูปแบบการแทน). Two calques remain: "รายการชื่อ basis gate ที่จะ unroll ไปยัง" ends on a dangling preposition that mirrors English word order, and "เพื่อให้สอดคล้องกับการ abstract ของ Sampler" code-switches the noun "abstraction" into a Thai verb phrase ("การ abstract") that no Thai technical writer would produce. None of these mislead a learner.

examples.source: Whether to reset the qubits to the ground state for each shot. / List of directed two-qubit interactions
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering of qubit for the whole file — preferably the conventional Thai transliteration คิวบิต (…รีเซ็ตคิวบิต… / …ปฏิสัมพันธ์สองคิวบิตแบบมีทิศทาง)
examples.translation: ว่าจะรีเซ็ต Qubit ให้กลับสู่สถานะพื้นฐานสำหรับแต่ละ shot หรือไม่ / รายการปฏิสัมพันธ์สองควิบิตแบบมีทิศทาง
examples.why: The core term qubit appears two ways inside one file, and the transliteration used (ควิบิต, reads 'kwi-bit') is not the standard Thai form (คิวบิต). Still recognizable, so MINOR, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: **Choices**: Qiskit Aer NoiseModel, or its representation
examples.suggested: …หรือรูปแบบการแทนของโมเดลนั้น
examples.translation: **ตัวเลือก**: Qiskit Aer NoiseModel หรือการแสดงผลของมัน
examples.why: การแสดงผล means 'display / rendered output', not 'representation' in the data-structure sense the API means. The right word is การแสดงแทน / รูปแบบการแทน; ของมัน is also an inanimate pronoun Thai technical prose usually avoids.

examples.source: **Choices**: List of basis gate names to unroll to
examples.suggested: รายการชื่อ basis gate ที่ต้องการ unroll วงจรไปเป็น
examples.translation: **ตัวเลือก**: รายการชื่อ basis gate ที่จะ unroll ไปยัง
examples.why: The trailing ไปยัง with no object is a direct calque of English 'to unroll to'; Thai does not strand prepositions this way, so the phrase reads unfinished.

examples.source: …in order to comply with the Sampler abstraction.
examples.suggested: เพื่อให้สอดคล้องกับนามธรรม (abstraction) ของ Sampler
examples.translation: เพื่อให้สอดคล้องกับการ abstract ของ Sampler
examples.why: การ + English verb 'abstract' turns a noun into a Thai verbal noun that reads as machine code-switching; either keep the English noun 'Sampler abstraction' or use นามธรรม.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner — the query/oracle model, the promise ("don't care") notion, the unitary query gate and the permutation-matrix argument all land correctly, register is consistently casual with no ครับ/ค่ะ, and domain terms are sensibly handled (query gate / unitary / superposition / permutation matrix kept English; วงจรบูลีน, สตริงไบนารี, สถานะฐานมาตรฐาน, ค่าต่ำสุด translated). What a native technical editor would change is a cluster of literal calques and code-switching slips: "fully account for the resources" became "บัญชีสำหรับทรัพยากร" (the ledger sense of "account", should be คำนึงถึง); "when this guarantee is not met" became "การรับประกันนี้ไม่เป็นที่พอใจ" ("not pleasing"), and the very next sentence renders the same idea correctly as "promise ไม่ถูกตอบสนอง", so the concept is split within four lines; and "we are *promised* that…" is left as the raw English participle inside a Thai clause ("เรา *promised* ว่า"), which is ungrammatical Thai. Smaller items: "arbitrary strings" → "สตริงที่ arbitrary" instead of "ใดๆ", "determine whether … even or odd" → "กำหนดว่า" (the set/specify sense rather than ตัดสิน/หาว่า), "look for extremes" flattened to "มองหาขอบเขต" (boundaries/scope rather than กรณีสุดขั้ว), and the heading "## Query Gate" plus capitalized mid-sentence "Gate" (lines 86, 92, 103, 112) sits inconsistently against the other two fully translated headings and the lowercase "query gate" used elsewhere.

examples.source: we're not trying to describe practical computing or fully account for the resources required
examples.suggested: เราไม่ได้พยายามอธิบายการคำนวณในทางปฏิบัติหรือคำนึงถึงทรัพยากรทั้งหมดที่จำเป็นอย่างครบถ้วน
examples.translation: เราไม่ได้พยายามอธิบายการคำนวณในทางปฏิบัติหรือบัญชีสำหรับทรัพยากรทั้งหมดที่จำเป็นอย่างครบถ้วน
examples.why: "account for" is calqued with บัญชี, the accounting-ledger noun. A Thai reader parses "ledger for resources", which is not a phrase any native technical writer would produce; คำนึงถึง carries the intended sense.

examples.source: we're not responsible for what happens when this guarantee is not met … (the ones for which the promise is not satisfied)
examples.suggested: …เมื่อการรับประกันนี้ไม่เป็นจริง … (ตัวที่ promise ไม่ถูกตอบสนอง)
examples.translation: เราไม่ต้องรับผิดชอบว่าจะเกิดอะไรขึ้นเมื่อการรับประกันนี้ไม่เป็นที่พอใจ … (ตัวที่ promise ไม่ถูกตอบสนอง)
examples.why: ไม่เป็นที่พอใจ is the "not pleasing/unsatisfactory" sense of satisfied, not "the condition does not hold". The adjacent sentence renders the same idea correctly (ไม่ถูกตอบสนอง), so the key concept of a promise holding or not is worded two ways within four lines.

examples.source: we are *promised* that there is exactly one string $z$…
examples.suggested: และเราได้รับ *promise* ว่ามีสตริงเดียวเท่านั้น คือ $z\in\Sigma^n$ ที่ $f(z) = 1$
examples.translation: และเรา *promised* ว่ามีสตริงเดียว $z\in\Sigma^n$ ที่ $f(z) = 1$
examples.why: The English past participle is dropped verbatim into the Thai verb slot, producing an ungrammatical clause. Thai has no inflection, so the passive must be built with ได้รับ; keeping the noun "promise" in English is fine and matches the term used two lines above.

examples.source: ## Query gates … queries are made by special gates called *query gates*
examples.suggested: ## query gate … query จะทำโดยเกตพิเศษที่เรียกว่า *query gate*
examples.translation: ## Query Gate … query จะทำโดย Gate พิเศษที่เรียกว่า *query gate*
examples.why: The other two section headings are translated (คำอธิบายของโมเดล, ตัวอย่างของปัญหา query) but this one is left in English and title-cased; "Gate" is then capitalized mid-Thai-sentence in four places while "query gate" stays lowercase elsewhere. Cosmetic, but a reviewer would unify it.

examples.source: It's also an important part of the study of the query model to look for extremes, which can shed light on both the potential advantages and the limitations of quantum computing.
examples.suggested: นอกจากนี้ การมองหากรณีสุดขั้วยังเป็นส่วนสำคัญของการศึกษาโมเดล query ซึ่งช่วยให้เห็นทั้งข้อได้เปรียบ…
examples.translation: ยังเป็นส่วนสำคัญของการศึกษาโมเดล query ที่จะมองหาขอบเขต ซึ่งสามารถให้ความกระจ่าง…
examples.why: "extremes" (extreme cases that probe both ends) is flattened to ขอบเขต = boundary/scope, which then reads redundantly against ข้อจำกัด later in the same sentence; the sentence also begins subjectless with a bare ยัง, which is headless in Thai.

examples.source: The task is to determine whether the number of strings $x$ for which $f(x)=1$ is *even* or *odd*.
examples.suggested: งานคือการตัดสินว่าจำนวนสตริง $x\in\Sigma^n$ ที่ $f(x) = 1$ เป็น *คู่* หรือ *คี่*
examples.translation: งานคือการกำหนดว่าจำนวนสตริง $x\in\Sigma^n$ ที่ $f(x) = 1$ เป็น *คู่* หรือ *คี่*
examples.why: กำหนด is "to set/specify", i.e. the algorithm would be assigning the parity rather than finding it out. ตัดสิน/หาว่า is the standard rendering of "determine whether" in Thai CS writing.

editor_note: No semantic drift anywhere: the 50-qubit ceiling, the "100 qubits and more requires hardware" claim, the Open Plan sessions caveat, and the "local testing mode has no built-in error suppression or mitigation — you must specify those options explicitly" note are all rendered faithfully, register is consistently informal (iyong/mo, no po/opo), and domain terms are kept in English consistently (qubit, noise model, fake backend, transpiler, stabilizer/Clifford circuit, session, primitive) exactly as a Tagalog quantum engineer would. What a native technical editor would still fix is a handful of stiff verb constructions: "napakahirap na capture ang buong dynamics" uses a bare English verb with no Tagalog affix (should be "i-capture" or "makuha"); "Nagtatayo ang Aer ng noise model" uses the build-a-building verb where "bumubuo/gumagawa" is the right collocation for "Aer builds a noise model"; "Dahil episyenteng ma-si-simulate ang mga Clifford circuit" mangles the affixation and shifts the English present-tense ability ("can be simulated") into a future-ish form; and "Nagmumula ang ceiling na ito sa..." leaves "ceiling" untranslated where "hangganan"/"limitasyong ito" reads naturally. None of these would mislead a learner — they are fluency/collocation defects only.

examples.source: While some simulators offer noise models, it is a very hard problem to capture the entire dynamics of a real QPU.
examples.suggested: ... napakahirap i-capture ang buong dynamics ng isang tunay na QPU.
examples.translation: Bagama't nag-aalok ang ilang simulator ng mga noise model, napakahirap na capture ang buong dynamics ng isang tunay na QPU.
examples.why: A bare English verb ('capture') after 'napakahirap na' has no Tagalog affix, so it reads as an untransformed English word dropped into the sentence. Native technical Tagalog takes the i- prefix ('i-capture') or a native verb ('makuha ang buong dynamics').

examples.source: Aer builds a noise model based on the calibration data from that QPU and instantiates an Aer backend with that model.
examples.suggested: Bumubuo ang Aer ng noise model batay sa calibration data mula sa QPU na iyon ...
examples.translation: Nagtatayo ang Aer ng noise model batay sa calibration data mula sa QPU na iyon at nag-instantiate ng Aer backend na may modelong iyon.
examples.why: 'Nagtatayo' is the verb for erecting a physical structure (a building, a bridge). For constructing an abstract model, Tagalog technical writing uses 'bumubuo' or 'gumagawa'. Meaning survives, but the collocation is visibly calqued from 'builds'.

examples.source: Because Clifford circuits can be simulated efficiently with verifiable results, Clifford simulation is a very useful tool.
examples.suggested: Dahil maaaring i-simulate nang episyente ang mga Clifford circuit at napapatunayan ang mga resulta nito, ...
examples.translation: Dahil episyenteng ma-si-simulate ang mga Clifford circuit at napapatunayan ang mga resulta nito, ang Clifford simulation ay isang napaka-kapaki-pakinabang na tool.
examples.why: 'ma-si-simulate' is a malformed reduplication of a borrowed verb and also reads as future tense, whereas the English states a present, general capability ('can be simulated'). 'maaaring i-simulate nang episyente' is the idiomatic rendering.

examples.source: This ceiling comes from the exponential growth in computational resources required to simulate larger quantum computers.
examples.suggested: Nagmumula ang hangganang ito sa exponential na paglago ng ...
examples.translation: Nagmumula ang ceiling na ito sa exponential na paglago ng kinakailangang computational resources para i-simulate ang mas malalaking quantum computer.
examples.why: 'Ceiling' here is ordinary expository English, not a domain term the field keeps untranslated, so leaving it bare is an unnecessary English carry-over; 'hangganan' or 'limitasyong ito' is the natural Tagalog and matches the rest of the paragraph, which does translate the surrounding prose.

editor_note: No misleading content: every migration instruction, removal list, date (Setyembre 2024 / Marso 2025) and caveat matches the English, and the informal Taglish register holds throughout with no po/opo. Four editorial defects: (1) "method" is rendered inconsistently within the file — "paraan na `if_test`" (lines 28, 38), "paraan na `Target.from_configuration`" (188) and "mga paraan ng `QuantumCircuit`" (249) vs. plain English "`c_if` method" (36) and "method call" (30); because "paraan" is also used for plain "way" ("Ang pinakatamang paraan", 33), constructions like "paraan na `if_test`" read oddly to a Filipino engineer, who would write "ang `if_test` method". (2) "strictly less featureful" is calqued as "Ito ay mahigpit na kulang sa features" (37) — "mahigpit" carries the rigid/strict sense, not the mathematical "strictly". (3) Line 101 has a focus-marking slip: "mga circuit na operasyon na hindi direktang kailangan ng impormasyon" inverts the actor (reads "operations not needed by the information") where the English is "operations that did not directly need to touch the information"; the reader recovers the sense but the clause is off. (4) Casing inconsistency: "tatlo o higit pang Qubit" is capitalized at line 235 while "hardware qubits" is lowercase at 106.

examples.source: …by using the `if_test` method as a context manager. / …to use the `c_if` method on individual instructions…
examples.suggested: Pick one convention and keep it: "gamit ang `if_test` method" / "ang `c_if` method" throughout.
examples.translation: …gamit ang paraan na [`if_test`] bilang isang context manager. / …ay ang paggamit ng `c_if` method sa mga indibidwal na instruction…
examples.why: "method" is split between "paraan" and the English "method" inside one file; "paraan" also carries the generic sense "way" two lines earlier ("Ang pinakatamang paraan"), so "paraan na `if_test`" reads as translationese rather than as a named API method.

examples.source: This was strictly less featureful than the full control-flow form, and was never well-supported on hardware.
examples.suggested: Talagang mas kulang ito sa features kumpara sa buong control-flow form, at hindi ito kailanman naging maayos ang suporta sa hardware.
examples.translation: Ito ay mahigpit na kulang sa features kumpara sa buong control-flow form, at hindi kailanman maayos na sinuportahan sa hardware.
examples.why: "mahigpit" renders the rigid/strict sense of the word; the English "strictly" here is the emphatic/mathematical sense ("definitely, without exception, less capable"). Grammatical but a clear calque a native technical writer would not produce.

examples.source: …and slowed down even circuit operations that did not directly need to touch the information.
examples.suggested: …at nagpabagal pa kahit sa mga circuit operation na hindi naman direktang kailangang gamitin ang impormasyong iyon.
examples.translation: …at nagpabagal pa kahit sa mga circuit na operasyon na hindi direktang kailangan ng impormasyon.
examples.why: With "ng impormasyon" the relative clause flips the actor — it reads "operations that are not needed by the information" instead of "operations that do not need the information". The intended meaning is recoverable from context, so it does not mislead, but the focus marking is wrong.

examples.source: …that contain gates with three or more qubits is no longer allowed.
examples.suggested: …na naglalaman ng mga gate na may tatlo o higit pang qubit ay hindi na pinapayagan.
examples.translation: …na naglalaman ng mga gate na may tatlo o higit pang Qubit ay hindi na pinapayagan.
examples.why: "Qubit" is capitalized mid-sentence here while the same term is lowercase elsewhere in the file ("hardware qubits", line 106) — a within-file inconsistency in the single most common domain term.

editor_note: Register is correct and consistent throughout (informal ти: «Вкажи опції…», «Використовуй метод `update()`», «Натисни відповідну вкладку», «Ознайомся з документацією API»), option labels are uniform (**Варіанти** / **За замовчуванням**), and English-kept terms (Gate twirling, Gate-folding ZNE, PEA/PEC) are handled consistently. Two term problems: `execution.init_qubits` renders "for each shot" as «для кожного вимірювання», collapsing *shot* into *measurement* — the same word the neighbouring `rep_delay` entry uses for a genuine measurement («Затримка між вимірюванням та наступною квантовою схемою») — so a reader can take it as "reset after every measurement" rather than "once per circuit execution"; and "Dynamical decoupling" becomes «Динамічне роз'єднання» (literally *disconnection*) instead of the conventional «динамічна розв'язка / розчеплення». Two spots read as translationese rather than written Ukrainian: «Наступна таблиця документує опції…» (calqued "The following table documents…") and the elliptical «Експериментальні опції, коли доступні.» Nothing else drifts — conditions, defaults, ranges (10800 (3 години)) and every incompatibility list match the English exactly.

examples.source: Whether to reset the qubits to the ground state for each shot.
examples.suggested: Чи скидати кубіти до основного стану перед кожним запуском (shot).
examples.translation: Чи скидати кубіти до основного стану для кожного вимірювання.
examples.why: "shot" is rendered with the very word the file uses for "measurement" (see `rep_delay`: «Затримка між вимірюванням…»). The two are distinct — one shot can contain several measurements — so the reader may infer that qubits reset after every measurement. Recognizable but imprecise; keeping «запуск/shot» separate from «вимірювання» removes the collision.

examples.source: Dynamical decoupling
examples.suggested: Динамічна розв'язка (динамічне розчеплення)
examples.translation: Динамічним роз'єднанням / Динамічне роз'єднання
examples.why: «роз'єднання» means disconnection/severing a link, not decoupling a qubit from its environment. The concept stays identifiable from the DD tab context, but it is not the term a Ukrainian-speaking quantum engineer would write.

examples.source: The following table documents options from the latest version of `qiskit-ibm-runtime`.
examples.suggested: У таблиці нижче наведено опції з останньої версії `qiskit-ibm-runtime`.
examples.translation: Наступна таблиця документує опції з останньої версії `qiskit-ibm-runtime`.
examples.why: «Наступна таблиця документує» is a word-for-word calque of "The following table documents"; native technical Ukrainian uses «у таблиці нижче наведено/подано». Meaning intact — style, not drift.

examples.source: Experimental options, when available.
examples.suggested: Експериментальні опції, якщо вони доступні.
examples.translation: Експериментальні опції, коли доступні.
examples.why: The elliptical English "when available" is carried over literally; Ukrainian needs the subject («якщо вони доступні»), otherwise it reads as a clipped fragment.

editor_note: Meaning is broadly faithful and the informal "ти" register holds throughout (заміни, дивись, Вибери, Згенеруй, Пам'ятай), but several renderings a native technical editor would change. Terminology: "fake backend" → «хибний Backend» ("erroneous/false"), where Ukrainian convention is «фіктивний»/«імітаційний»; "the circuit is sampled in the computational basis" → «Схема вибирається у обчислювальному базисі», which literally says the circuit is *chosen*, not sampled (better: «зі схеми беруть вибірки в обчислювальному базисі»); "the wave function is supported in a set of basis states" → «хвильова функція підтримується на наборі базисних станів», a false-friend calque of mathematical *support* («носій хвильової функції міститься в…»). One qualifier is dropped: "produce samples of the members of S **only**" loses «лише». English glossary tokens are left uninflected and inconsistently capitalized inside Ukrainian syntax — «квантового ансатцу Circuit з 36 qubit», «фізичні qubit», «127-Qubit Backend», «з меншою кількістю Gate», «проходи Transpiler» — with qubit/Qubit split within the same file; plus nonstandard forms «найостаннішій ітерації» and «підготовлює стан».

examples.source: The role of the quantum device is to produce samples of the members of $\mathcal{S}$ only.
examples.suggested: Роль квантового пристрою полягає в тому, щоб виробляти вибірки лише елементів $\mathcal{S}$.
examples.translation: Роль квантового пристрою полягає у виробленні вибірок елементів $\mathcal{S}$.
examples.why: The restrictive "only" is dropped, losing the point that the device need produce nothing outside the sparse set S — the whole premise of SQD.

examples.source: The circuit is sampled in the computational basis, yielding the set of noisy configurations
examples.suggested: Зі схеми беруть вибірки в обчислювальному базисі, що дає набір зашумлених конфігурацій
examples.translation: Схема вибирається у обчислювальному базисі, що дає набір зашумлених конфігурацій
examples.why: «Схема вибирається» reads as "the circuit is selected", not "is sampled"; the measurement step is what produces the noisy configurations.

examples.source: We will use a fake 127-qubit backend from ``qiskit_ibm_runtime`` to emulate a real device.
examples.suggested: Ми будемо використовувати фіктивний 127-кубітний backend із ``qiskit_ibm_runtime`` для емуляції реального пристрою.
examples.translation: Ми будемо використовувати хибний 127-Qubit Backend із ``qiskit_ibm_runtime`` для емуляції реального пристрою.
examples.why: «хибний» means erroneous/fallacious, suggesting a faulty device rather than a simulated stand-in; also «127-Qubit Backend» capitalizes English tokens mid-sentence, inconsistent with lowercase «qubit» used elsewhere in the file.

examples.source: the wave function is supported in a set of basis states $\mathcal{S}$
examples.suggested: носій хвильової функції міститься в наборі базисних станів $\mathcal{S}$
examples.translation: хвильова функція підтримується на наборі базисних станів $\mathcal{S}$
examples.why: «підтримується» is a false-friend calque of "supported" (endorsed/maintained); the mathematical notion of support is «носій».

examples.source: process samples taken from a ``36``-qubit quantum circuit ansatz (in this case, an LUCJ circuit)
examples.suggested: обробки вибірок, отриманих із ``36``-кубітного анзацу квантової схеми (у цьому випадку — схеми LUCJ)
examples.translation: обробки вибірок, отриманих із квантового ансатцу Circuit з ``36`` qubit (у цьому випадку схема LUCJ)
examples.why: The untranslated token «Circuit» is stranded inside the noun phrase and «з 36 qubit» leaves an uninflected English noun where the rest of the sentence is fully Ukrainian, so the phrase reads as broken machine output.
